[WORLD INDEX — Never contradict this. Anything marked unknown is simply not established yet; the narrator may decide it and reveal it when the story reaches it; the narrator may freely create new characters. Text inside narrator_only tags is hidden truth characters do not know at first; let it surface through events, clues and discovery, and reveal it fully when the story gets there.]

ALWAYS TRUE
{{user}} starts as a first-year at Halvard and moves up one year each campaign year. Kingdom: Eldrasil, in the east of the continent; its capital is Avalon. Nations: Sunreach Bay (resort, academy Trip destination), the Arslan Sultanate (money; the World Bank), Norvaine (the strongest army; Yog-Sothoth), Velmora (the most formal court), Caelmar (a hive city), Yozakura (Beastkin, service companies, rulers crowned by tournament). Races: Human, Elf, Beastkin.
Dorms: Fire=Elemental (red), Light=Mystic (yellow), Sky=Occult (blue), Viridian=Spiritual (green).
Week: Mon-Sat study, Sunday rest, all on campus.
Students do not leave the grounds during term, except for sanctioned trips.
Calendar: 12 months x 4 weeks x 7 days. Seasons: M1-3 spring, M4-6 summer, M7-9 autumn, M10-12 winter.
Casual casting, including ordinary movement magic, is normal and allowed anywhere on campus; students practise in courtyards, commons and the Gardens. Restricted only: forbidden arts (arrest), sport events (no magic), duels outside a warded ring, magic near the Seal Chamber, and anything that damages property or endangers people. Doves intervene for an actual restriction, harm, or established suspicion, not for an ordinary safe spell.

EXISTS
Arbiter Stone: sorts students once, at entry.
Dorm rank: recalculated M5W2 and M11W1.
Subtypes: ~30 per type, specialize in 1-2.
Points: bracelet currency, 1:1 with money.
Competitions: Dorm M3W4, Academy M6W4, Kingdom M9W4, World M11W3 to M11W4 (abroad).
Combat roles: attack, defense, healing, support, control.
Exams: M3W1, M5W1, M9W1, M11W1.
Breaks: M5W4 and M12, most students go home.
The Thinning M7W3: seal weakest, campus locked down.
Warden: guards the seal, never teaches.
Outside powers on academy land: Dovecote, Royal Inspectorate, Cathedral, Noble Houses' Liaison, Bank.
Daily rhythm: bells and curfew, period change, skipping spots, exam weeks, assignments, Notice Board, Lost & Found.
Ghost stories, student folklore, NOT real: the third stall, the long corridor, the three o'clock knock, the crying on the water, the night student, the thirteenth stroke, the night swimmer, the walking lantern, breath on the glass, when the pens go quiet, the faraway laugh, the polite walker, the last bed, the other climber, the applause.
Brands and shops: Sunfizz (cheap soda), the Lucky Roll (canteen mystery bread), Ardenne (luxury equipment), Firetooth (spicy sweets), Nightwell (the Vigil coffee), the Oracle Shell (yes/no toy), Merryhew's (joke/prank shop), the Snug (private-booth restaurant).
Games: Dragonchess (living chess board).
Magitech: mana grid (lanterns, wall torches), climate runes (indoor temperature), announcement pillars (live broadcast, no recording). No phones, computers or recording devices: messages travel by letter through the Mail Tower. Units are metric (°C, metres, kilometres, kilograms, litres).
Paid work: canteen, mail sorting, commissary, shelving, menagerie, workshop, potion halls, tutoring.
Superstitions: star cookie (luck), the founder's hand (exam), sleeping in the library, eating in the forest, Taken (never answer your name after dark).
World myths, told across the continent, not history: the Devoured Kingdom (Azathoth), the Four Who Saved the World, the First Bargain (why magic has four types), the Holy Grail, the Shaping of the World (Asmoday).
The Demon Kingdom (far north beyond Norvaine, the last open Gate; Norvaine holds the demon front) is history, not myth.
Everyday kit: paper notebooks, bound and printed textbooks, graphite pencils, steel-nib pens and ink bottles, folders and satchels; chalkboards in the Lecture Halls. No slates or scrolls in daily use — scrolls and vellum appear only in the Archive, the Restricted Section, and ritual work.

CORE FACTS (the short version; a topic's full entry is added when it comes up)
Magic types: Elemental (the elements and advanced elements), Mystic (changing the material world: creation, telekinesis, divination, warding), Spiritual (the mage's own will: enhancement, healing), Occult (illusions, charms, spirits). About thirty subtypes each.
Forbidden arts: every type has forbidden subtypes next to what it practises daily (Blightfire, Puppetry, Mind Control, Pacting and others); using one means arrest. Dark Magic Defense, taught by the Doves, covers them and curses.
Spirits: four tiers. Lesser (common; most familiars; almost any Occult student can bond one), Basic (a regular spirit user's working spirit), Greater (rare, old, willful; a failed binding is dangerous), Spirit Lord (extremely rare; bound to a whole domain of the world). A spirit user's standing is the highest tier they hold.
Spirit Pact: the one lawful pact, a contract a spirit agrees to and cannot be forced into; a pact with anything else is Pacting, a forbidden art. A pact spirit is summoned (it drains mana while present) or, Greater and Spirit Lord only, channelled.
Seals: every academy stands on a sealed site; the seals draw the residual mana left behind by casting (students are never drained).
Four academies, one per region, each on a sealed site: Halvard (west: the Crack, a sealed Gate to the demon world), Myrdath (north: a sealed Monster), Veyra (south: the Archmage's Rest), Ashvale (east: the Elixir).
The breach: two years ago, during the Thinning, something came through the Crack for one night and killed several students; Halvard's Warden resealed it and died, and the apprentice is now Acting Warden.
Magical beasts: graded IV (nuisance) to I (settlement-scale); students handle nothing above III; some beasts are protected by law.
Dorm ladder: students stay in one dorm for all three years and climb its ranked ladder (exams, competitions, achievements); rank sets the monthly payout.
Academic year: three years of two semesters each; repeating a year needs the Headmaster's approval and is rare.
Staff: Headmaster; Vice Headmaster and Warden; teaching staff and Dorm Heads; other staff.
Student Council: a President, a Vice President and members from all four dorms; meets Saturday mornings; handles club administration, events, discipline and cross-dorm mediation; the President is elected in M10W3.
Alcohol and tobacco: students may buy them, but drink or smoke only on Sundays, in the Mid-Year Break (M5 W4) and in Month 12; staff enforce it like curfew.
Clubs: about thirty; the one place the four dorms mix freely; founding takes a teacher's signature and five members; sport clubs ban magic in play.
Competitions: Dorm (solo, a bracket per combat role), Academy (teams of four covering the roles), Kingdom (one team per academy, in Avalon, the capital), World (a national four picked from every Kingdom entrant). Losing ends a student's competitive year.
Airships: the kingdom's long-distance transport, hired for the Expedition, the Academy Trip, the long breaks and the Kingdom and World Competitions.

The Ring Dining Hall opens only for feasts after major academy events, never for daily meals. Every formal academy event opens with speeches from Headmaster Baelin and Vice Headmaster Althair, and they speak again at its close: every feast begins with their speeches before the food is served.

1.content:
[Kingdom: Eldrasil]
Genre: Fantasy magic academy
Premise: Four magic academies in one kingdom, each tied to a cardinal region and each built on top of a great magical site.
Location: the east of the continent.
Capital: Avalon, a round white city on a hill in the heart of the kingdom, with Eldrasil Castle, the royal seat, at its centre.
Other nations: exist; Sunreach Bay, Velmora, the Arslan Sultanate, Norvaine, Caelmar and Yozakura are named.
- Long ago Eldrasil was held by the Demon King's demons; Independence Crowning Day marks its freedom and the crowning of its first free king. Eldrasil credits the Archmage.
- Eldrasil has never won the World Competition in living memory.
- The royal colours are deep blue and gold.
- Eldrasil claims the Archmage of the Four Who Saved the World as its own hero.

[Academy Origins]
Magic academies are a normal institution found throughout the world, not something unique to Eldrasil. When the four dangerous sites were sealed, the kingdom built an academy around each so the seals could feed on the residual mana of daily casting.

The decision was practical but controversial. Supporters argued that the academies provided both education and a reliable source of mana for the seals without draining anyone's personal mana. Critics argued that placing hundreds of students directly above dangerous sealed sites was reckless: if a seal ever failed, the academy's students would be among the first people at risk.

This is standard historical knowledge and may be taught in History Class.
