5.content:
[Halvard Academy]
Region: West. Site: The Crack, one of the old Gates to the demon world, sealed by the Archmage; the crack in reality is what the seal left. Site name unknown.
Headmaster: an Elf, head of Halvard for forty years.
Local fear: the Crack itself and whatever might come through it. Rumours about it are the academy's favourite ghost stories, and anything unusual (a strange mark, odd eyes, horns) invites whispers.
The breach: two years ago, during The Thinning, something came through for a single night and killed several students before Halvard's Warden resealed the Crack, dying in the act. The Warden's apprentice inherited the seal that night and the crown has only ever confirmed them as Acting Warden. What it was has never been described publicly and survivors disagree about what they saw. Current third-years lived through it as first-years. Afterwards the Headmaster hired a veteran monster hunter to teach Creature Studies. The dead are honoured on Remembrance Day (M10W1), and the Doves interrogated survivors afterwards, which many students have never forgiven.

6.content:
The Student Council meets on Saturday mornings, 10:00-12:00, in the Student Council Chamber, in place of its members' Study Hall; members keep their own clubs in the 13:00-16:00 block. Students with an F attend their required remedial instead. It has a President, a Vice President, and members from each of the four dorms; there is no fixed membership limit. Together they handle club administration, events, student discipline, cross-dorm mediation, and speaking for students to staff.
The President is elected each year in Month 10 Week 3: campaigning Monday-Thursday, a debate after Friday classes in the Seminar Rooms, and voting in the Main Courtyard during Saturday's club block. The President-elect names the losing candidate Vice President-elect. The serving leaders keep their authority through Graduation; the successors take office at the start of the next school year. Membership alone grants neither disciplinary immunity nor executive authority.

7.content:
- Seals feed on mana. Academies were built on the sites because a place full of mages releases the most mana.
- Warden duty: Checking and monitoring mana consumption.

Magic leaves residual mana in the environment after a spell is cast. Normally this residual mana disperses and naturally fades over time. The seals draw this otherwise unusable residual mana toward the sealed site before it dissipates.

Students are not living mana batteries and are not deliberately drained by the academy. The seal only collects mana that has already been spent and left behind by casting.

9.content:
[The Thinning]
Why: the seal stores residual mana like a reservoir while whatever it holds presses against it in a yearly cycle peaking in Month 7. The busy second half of the year fills the reserve; the Month 12 holiday drains it; the first half refills it slowly and the Mid-Year Break empties the campus again. During both long breaks a skeleton staff and the Warden stay to keep the seal fed.
Rules: absolute curfew, academy locked, nobody outside. The lockdown keeps hundreds of students away from vulnerable areas in case of a breach.
- The wards along the outer wall flicker faintly all week, and the birds leave the grounds until it is over.
Mood: a week of hearing things through the walls.

10.content:
[Academy Staff]
Hierarchy:
- Tier 1: Headmaster (1 per academy)
- Tier 2: Vice Headmaster, Warden (1 per academy)
- Tier 3: Teaching Staff, Dorm Heads
- Tier 4: Other Staff
Teaching staff: Teach the academy classes. Magic Theory, History, Etiquette and Potion Crafting have a different teacher for each year level. Creature Studies and the five Practical Magic classes (one per combat role) have one teacher each for all three years. Dark Magic Defense is taught by the Doves, who are not academy staff, to every year. The Headmaster and the Vice Headmaster teach a class each as well (second-year History, third-year Magic Theory).
Free periods: now and then a teacher cannot come (called away, ill, a meeting, an emergency); the class is not held, it counts against no one, and the hour is free.
Club duty: Each teacher is responsible for exactly one club. A club requires a teaching staff signature to found.

11.content:
[The Warden]
Count: One per site, four in the kingdom total.
Duties:
- Maintaining the site's seal
- Guarding the site from trespassers
Nature of the seal: Every site seal was laid by the Archmage. No living mage could build one, and none is asked to. A seal is a standing working that can be read, tuned, patched and re-anchored by anyone who understands how it runs, which is what a Warden is trained for. Sealing affinity helps but is not the post's requirement; knowing the working is.
Notes: The original wardens were historical figures tied to the founding era of the academies. The modern Warden is a single successor at each site.

At Halvard: The previous Warden (name unknown) died resealing the Crack on the breach night two years ago. Their apprentice took over the seal that night. The crown has never confirmed them as full Warden, only Acting Warden, because they answer to no one and do whatever they judge necessary.

12.content:
[Dorms]
Structure: Four dorms per academy, sorted by magic type, each in its own building that admits only its own students. Students stay in that dorm for all three years. Within each dorm, students climb a ranked ladder, recalculated twice a year from exams, competition results, and achievements; a student's current rank sets their monthly point payout.
Buildings: four identical grey-stone buildings around the Main Courtyard, told apart by roof colour and one feature each; doors open only to residents' bracelets. Each dorm's Dorm Head lives in the building with its students.
Types:
- Elemental: The four elements — fire, water, wind, earth — and advanced elements such as ice, lightning, metal, etc.
- Mystic: Magic that changes the material world: creating objects, telekinesis, divination. Includes astral magic.
- Spiritual: Magic drawing on the mage's force of will: enhancing the mage, healing.
- Occult: Illusions, charms, and binding spirits.

17.content:
Magic Theory Class
Purpose: Teach students why magic works, not just how — the underlying structure of mana, why seals consume it, and why the four types behave differently. Grounds every other class.
Activity: Lectures with diagrams of mana flow. Written analysis of failed spells. Students invent and defend original spell theories. Occasional joint sessions where all four dorms compare how they'd solve the same problem.
Covers: residual mana and the seal, the four magic types and their subtypes (Elemental magic, Mystic magic, Spiritual magic, Occult magic), Spirit Pact and Spirit Tiers.
The First Bargain is the folk answer to why magic has four types; Magic Theory teaches the structure and leaves the story to Dark Magic Defense.

18.content:
[Academic Structure]
Duration: 3 years, 6 semesters total, 2 semesters per year.
Full holiday month: 12. Month 12 is a full holiday for the whole kingdom; the World Competition abroad is in Month 11, from Week 3 Monday to Week 4 Monday, before Graduation.
Repeating a year: A student may repeat one year of study with the Headmaster's approval, usually after illness, injury, or a breakdown. It is rare and noticed.
Magic shows itself in childhood. The gifted enroll at 18 for formal training; nobody's magic 'awakens' on arrival.
Students routinely copy notes and finish assignments in the last minutes before a bell; being five minutes late can mean arriving to a closed classroom door.

19.content:
[Competitions]
Four tiers, elimination. Losing at any tier ends your competitive year. The one exception is World selection, which is chosen rather than won.
1. Dorm. Solo, open to the whole dorm, in five brackets, one per combat role, each judged by that role's Practical Magic teacher: Attack is a knockout duel; Defense holds a ring against rising attacks, longest standing wins; Healing races to treat staged injuries, judged on speed and precision; Support is paired at random with an Attack fighter of the same dorm and judged on that partner's bout; Control is a duel won by holding the opponent still for ten seconds, no injury needed. Every entrant finishes with a placement. Sixteen per dorm qualify for the Academy Competition by role, whoever goes furthest in their bracket: Attack 4, Defense 3, Healing 3, Support 3, Control 3; winning is not required. Each bracket's champion earns 100 points and its runner-up 50.
2. Academy. Qualifiers from all four dorms form teams of 4 in the weeks before, with at least one student from each year level, covering the combat roles (attack, defense, healing, support, control) between them. Teams mix dorms and usually must, since no dorm covers every role well. Knockout bracket; the winning team represents the academy.
3. Kingdom. One team per academy, four in total, over three rounds in and around Avalon, the capital. Every competitor wears a ward seal; when it breaks they are pulled out for the rest of the round. Round one, outdoors in the Kingsmeadow beyond the city wall: from morning each team hunts for a Kingsbloom, and only three are planted; the judges take one per team at sunset, and the team without one goes out. Round two, in the Undercroft beneath the Royal Arena: ten rooms, each guarded by a bound beast; a team takes a room by defeating its beast and then being the only team inside for fifteen minutes, one member is enough, and the count stops while anyone from another team is in the room; a taken room can be taken again the same way. The two teams that hold four rooms at the same time go through. Round three, the final, on the arena sand: one team against the other. Great scrying crystals over the arena show the crowd the rounds fought away from the sand. Each member of the winning team earns 5,000 points, and the winning team is received by the King at Eldrasil Castle on the last evening. Only the teams travel: they arrive the day before and stay at the Whitestone Hotel beside the arena, and fly home the day after. Evenings are free in the city until 21:00, the hotel by 22:00. Halvard's team goes with Gavlan Haverton as its escort; the rest of the academy stays at school and follows the news.
4. World (abroad), Month 11 Week 3 Monday to Week 4 Monday. A panel builds the national 4 from the best individuals for the combat roles across all Kingdom participants, winners and losers alike, with no year-level requirement. Being picked off a losing team is a great honour. Six nations compete: four hold a standing invitation (Eldrasil, Yozakura, Norvaine and Caelmar), and two places go to an open qualification earlier in the year, which the Arslan Sultanate and Velmora have won in recent years ahead of Sunreach Bay and the rest. Yozakura, Norvaine and Caelmar are the usual favourites, and Yozakura won the competition before campaign Year 1. Eldrasil has never won in living memory. Every nation's four travels with a coach; Eldrasil's is Gavlan Haverton, as at the Kingdom.
Picked to fight together: in the competition before campaign Year 1, Gareth Valkaryn and Lucius Vortigern were the strongest in Eldrasil on paper; on the field Lucius's swarm ate Gareth's fire, and Yozakura took the title. Since then, at Gavlan Haverton's urging, the panel picks the four for how they fight together, not only for who is strongest.
Format: an opening banquet on arrival, where the Phase 1 groups are drawn; Phase 1 (below); Phase 2, two head-to-head matches on two days, the losers going out; a rest day; Phase 3, the Grand Final in the arena, the only straight team-against-team fight, then the closing banquet.
Phase 1 (two days, one group of three teams each day): Last Team Standing in a forest bounded by a barrier that shrinks all match long. Every competitor is teleported to a random spot, alone, and carries a crystal; when it breaks, that competitor is out. The first team to lose every member is out of the competition. The match runs until one team is left: it tops the group and is the top seed in Phase 2, and the other survivor goes through second.
Phase 2 (two days, one match a day): Siege, in an old fortress with two ward stones. The attacking team carries one Breach Rune, a siege working: planted on a ward stone with a minute of unbroken channelling, it fills for three minutes and then breaks the stone. A defender can unwind a planted rune with a minute of unbroken channelling of their own. Attackers win a round when the stone breaks or every defender is out; defenders win when they unwind the rune, when ten minutes pass without a planting, or when every attacker is out before one. Crystals work as in Phase 1 and are replaced each round; healing cannot mend a broken crystal. The first team to win four rounds goes to the Grand Final; the sides swap after the third round, and at three all a seventh round decides. The top seed chooses its first side and the side in a seventh round.
Prize: each member of the winning four earns 10,000 points and takes home a small replica of the World Trophy; the trophy itself stays with the winning nation until the next competition. Yozakura held it when campaign Year 1 began.
The World Competition moves each year between the four invited nations. (Campaign Year 1) This year Yozakura hosts it, in its capital, Hanakaze; a Yozakuran liner flies the teams there in half a day. (Campaign Year 2) This year Caelmar hosts it. (Campaign Year 3) This year it comes home to Eldrasil, in Avalon. The teams lodge together, and evenings are free in the city until 21:00, back by 22:00.

20.content:
[Point System]
Balances are private by default, though anyone may show theirs.
Sources: a monthly payout by current dorm rank (300 at the bottom band up to 3,000 for a dorm's rank 1); paid work; academic marks; competition results, where a Kingdom Competition win pays 5,000, more than most students earn in half a year.
Family money converts at the Banking House.
Everything in the mall costs points, from a 15-point bakery roll to a 4,000-point quality focus, while a free version of nearly everything exists on campus: the canteen against the restaurants, the common-room kettle against the cafés, self-service laundry against the paid service.
Effect: wealth is visible without being announced. A student who never eats at the mall is marked by the habit, and since rare reagents cost more than a bottom-band student earns in a month, those who can afford good materials earn the marks that pay for more.

21.content:
[Entrance Event]
When: Month 1 Week 1 Monday
- 07:00-09:00 Arrival: new students check in at Reception and Gatehouse.
- 09:00 Ceremony in the Arbiter Hall: Headmaster Baelin and Vice Headmaster Althair address the new class before sorting begins. The first-years then touch the Arbiter Stone one by one. Immediately after each sorting, a Student Council member gives that student the vest of their new dorm; they sit with that dorm and remain in the hall until everyone is sorted at 10:00. Do not send a sorted first-year outside to wait or offer free time between their sorting and the end of the ceremony.
- 10:00-18:00 Tour: after sorting ends, each group is exactly two new first-years and one senior. The assigned trio meets in the Arbiter Hall and tours the campus together; club booths are stops along the way. Keep the same trio until the tour ends. Use the recorded Campus_State.Entrance_tour assignment; choose available roster students of this year's entering cohort before inventing a new first-year, and a roster senior before inventing a guide. If every suitable roster student is unavailable, a narrator-created student may fill the place.
- Club promotion: stands across the academy, 10:00-18:00 on sorting day, then every afternoon after classes (16:00-18:00) until Friday; registration closes Friday at 18:00. It opens on sorting day on purpose, so clubs recruit before dorm loyalty settles.
- Late afternoon: seniors show new students their rooms inside the dorms.
- 19:00 Entrance Feast in the Ring Dining Hall: Headmaster Baelin and Vice Headmaster Althair speak again before dinner is served.
From {{user}}'s second year: {{user}} is a returning student: sorted in their first year and never sorted again. Today {{user}} is one of the seniors: at 10:00 {{user}} meets the two assigned new first-years in Campus_State.Entrance_tour and takes them round the whole campus until 18:00 (their questions, the shortcuts, the places to avoid, the club booths on the way), and in the late afternoon shows them their rooms if they were sorted into {{user}}'s dorm. {{user}} watches the speeches and sorting from the gallery, and eats at the Entrance Feast with their own year.

22.content:
[Star Night]
When: Month 1 Week 3 Saturday, sunset to sunrise. No 8pm curfew.
- Night market near the grassy fields, 8pm to midnight, run by students and mall vendors.
- Students stargaze on the Grassy Field and Hills and sleep outside in tents or bedrolls.
- Astral magic (Mystic) is at its strongest.
- The sky is unnaturally clear: every star visible as if through a telescope.
- Midnight peak: a great meteor shower. A wish made during it is believed to come true.
- Far to the north, the same midnight is the one Norvaine dreads: the night Yog-Sothoth takes its Chosen.

23.content:
[Dorm Days]
When: Sundays, one dorm each. Spiritual M1W4, Mystic M4W3, Elemental M8W4, Occult M10W2.
Open house: the dorm opens to the other three, usually the only time outsiders see inside. The common room displays the dorm's history, and the founding warden is honoured with a small rite at the entrance.
Day: upperclassmen showcase casting in the courtyard; first-years run booths; a public lesson lets outsiders try the dorm's type badly, for laughs. Food stalls sell the traditional dish, sweets and charms to fund the year; visiting dorms bring a food gift (a quiet competition). Type contests (precision, endurance, control) are open to all, plus a dorm-internal tournament with useless but prestigious prizes and no ranking effect.
Evening: dorm-only closing dinner; first-years formally welcomed and given a token of belonging; dorm-specific lights, lanterns or music.

24.content:
[Independence Crowning Day]
When: Month 4 Week 2, Tuesday. Kingdom holiday for independence and the ruler's crowning. No classes.
What it marks: the day, long ago, Eldrasil was freed from demon rule and crowned its own king.
The day before: students change bracelet points into coin at the Banking House; points do not work in the capital.
Morning: Headmaster Baelin and Vice Headmaster Althair speak to the assembled academy at 07:00, then everyone boards the airship to Avalon, the capital (about two hours).
Avalon: the airship lands at the Skyport at 09:30. 10:00 the parade on Crown Avenue, the Royal Mages at its head, watched from the stands reserved for Halvard; 11:00 the King's speech at Crown Square, carried by the Herald Spires to the whole city. Then free time from 11:30 until the muster at the Skyport at 15:30 (markets, food, sights; the city's own entries). Groups of four only. Points do not work; students carry coin.
Late afternoon: the airship leaves at 16:00, back before dark, passenger lists counted twice. A student late for the muster is searched for, and punished as for a detention.
Night: fireworks over the lake, bursting beyond Willow Island and doubled in the water, watched from the Grassy Field and Hills and the shore; curfew moves to 10pm.
The royal banners, deep blue and gold, fly from the castle towers all day; that night the hired airship rides at anchor at the edge of the grounds, beyond the Menagerie and the Gymnasium.
Rules: uniform all day; the Doves travel along and staff count heads constantly.

25.content:
[Academy Founder Day]
When: Month 9 Week 3, Saturday. Marks the founding of Halvard. No classes.
Morning: speeches from the Headmaster and Vice Headmaster in the Arbiter Hall, then a short rite at the Founder's Statue.
Treasure hunt: optional, solo or group. Everyone gets the same first clue; each solved clue leads to the next across the whole campus.
Origin: the founding warden hid the academy's charter and refused to teach until the first students found it: a mage who cannot think is only a weapon.
Status: notoriously hard, rewritten by staff each year; nobody has finished in years, and the prize is never announced.
Evening: the Headmaster and Vice Headmaster speak, then the feast in the Ring Dining Hall.

26.content:
[Clubs]
Count: around thirty, uncapped. Founding: a teaching staff signature and five members. One teacher is responsible for one club.
Sport and duelling clubs also practise informally after 16:00 on other days. Outside sport clubs, clubs use magic freely as their activity requires.
Cross-dorm: clubs are the one place the four magic types mix freely, because recruitment happens before dorm loyalty settles.
Members not named elsewhere are unnamed students.
Sport clubs ban magic outright during play, which is why they feed directly into Sports Day.
Note: the Magic Duelling Club is spell duelling inside warded rings, never swordplay, staves or fistfights. Practice with spells also stays in the rings.

27.content:
History Class
Purpose: Cover the Archmage, the original wardens, the founding of the four academies, and Eldrasil's independence. Justifies why the academy system exists.
Activity: Lectures and reading. Debates on contested events. Essays on a historical mage. Field visits to monuments on academy grounds, especially before Remembrance Day.
Covers: the Archmage and the original wardens, the Gates and Eldrasil's rule by the demons, independence, the founding of the four academies, and the academy records in the Archive.
Draws the line between myth and record: the Gates, the demons' rule over Eldrasil, the Demon Kingdom and the Archmage's seals are history; the First Bargain and the Four Who Saved the World are legend.

28.content:
Etiquette Class
Purpose: Turn powerful children into civilized mages. Magic gives a student the power to hurt, coerce, or take, and this is the one class that asks what they owe the people around them. Covers ethics, personal conduct, and enough psychology to recognise pressure, manipulation, and one's own worst impulses. The academy's quiet answer to the question of why graduates become healers and guards rather than criminals, dark mages, or cultists.
Activity: Moral dilemmas argued aloud, with students made to defend the side they disagree with. Case studies of mages who crossed the line, and how each of them started. Restraint drills: winning an argument without magic, refusing a request, de-escalating a fight. Lessons on consent, duty of care, and helping without being asked. Applied conduct: correspondence, titles and address, dining, and mock receptions, since graduates serve noble houses and Graduation is attended by nobles.
Marked on judgement and conduct, not politeness. A student can be flawless at a reception and still fail.
Covers: personal ethics, the legal line each type sits near (see Dark Magic Defense), the Noble Houses' Liaison, and conduct at Graduation. Its lessons on noble conduct follow Velmoran court manners, the continent's standard.

29.content:
Creature Studies Class
Purpose: Identification, handling, and extermination of magical beast.
Activity: Handling live specimens in the academy menagerie. Field identification walks. Written bestiary work. Supervised capture and release. The Month 2 expedition is the practical exam.
Covers: beast grades I to IV, protected beasts, the Menagerie, and the Creature Studies Expedition.

30.content:
[Practical Magic]
Formerly called Combat Class; students still say "Combat".
Purpose: Practical casting under pressure, taught by combat role. The direct feeder into all four competition tiers.
Classes: five, one per combat role, each with one teacher for all three years: Attack (Gavlan Haverton, Combat Grounds), Defense (Anselm Graywater, the Sparring Pavilion), Healing (Hester Mortlake, the Healing Ward of the Medical Centre), Support (Magnus Tarrant, Combat Grounds), Control (Dorian Pryce, Combat Grounds). All five meet at the same time, Monday and Thursday afternoons; a role class mixes the four dorms and is taught by year.
Roles: a student attends the class of their combat role; a student with two roles picks the one they want most. The first class of the year (Month 1 Week 1 Thursday) is a joint assessment: the five teachers watch the first-years in drills and assign their roles.
Activity: Spellcasting drills, sparring and duels, marked by the role's own standard. Sparring partners come from one's own dorm except in Training Week; this is a class rule, not a ban on casting elsewhere.
Covers: the five combat roles, and preparation for the Dorm and Academy Competitions.

31.content:
Potion Crafting
Purpose: Give students a method that works without spending mana, and produce healers. Each dorm's approach differs by type.
Activity: Brewing to recipe, then independent formulation. Reagent identification and storage. Harvest-linked practicals. Failed batches disposed of under supervision.
Covers: the Potion Halls, reagents from the Gardens, healing draughts, and where the line to Poison magic sits.

32.content:
Dark Magic Defense
Purpose: Recognize, survive, and counter the forbidden magic, and know exactly where the legal line sits in your own type, since each of the four types has a forbidden art neighboring something it practices daily; and countermeasures against whatever leaks from the sites. The most serious class in the curriculum. Taught not by academy teachers but by Doves from the Dovecote.
Activity: Curse identification and breaking, since Effigy leaves no evidence. Counter-warding against specific arts. Detection work on the undetectable half of the list, reading behavior and aftermath rather than residue. Legal boundary drills taught per dorm. Defensive drills against staff-cast approximations. The lesson on Pacting opens with the First Bargain.
Dark Magic Defense teaches how to recognise and survive the forbidden arts; Etiquette teaches why people reach for them in the first place. The two classes are deliberately paired.
The twenty forbidden arts (not all, but the famous one), by type. Elemental: Blightfire, Salting, Poison magic, Rot magic, Weather change magic. Mystic: Unmaking, Puppetry, Wringing, Soul magic, Raise dead. Spiritual: Burning magic, Drawing magic, Mind control, Slavery magic, Effigy. Occult: Demon summoning, Forbidden charm, Pacting, Wearing magic, Blood magic.

33.content:
Elemental — Subtypes († = forbidden: harm that outlives the caster)
Standard: Fire, Water, Wind, Earth, Ice, Lightning, Metal, Magma, Sand, Crystal, Acid, Mud, Ash, Snow, Steam, Mist, Smoke, Wood, Storm, Sound, Oil, Obsidian, Clay, Magnetism, Salt.
Notes: Light — raw light, flashes and glare; not holy, unrelated to the Light Dormitory. Dark — absorbing light and warmth; not evil.
Blightfire†: fire that never goes out, poisoning land for generations. Salting†: permanently killing soil, unlike ordinary Salt. Poison†: toxins made to persist and spread, unlike Potion Crafting. Rot†: decay that eats land and stone permanently. Weather†: changing weather on a scale no one can control.

34.content:
Mystic — Subtypes († = forbidden: treating people and souls as material)
Standard: Creation, Telekinesis, Teleportation, Barrier, Gravity, Mending, Reinforcement, Duplication, Divination, Scrying, Portal, Transmutation, Resizing, Enchantment, Golemancy, Dispelling, Phasing, Warding.
Notes: Object Reading — an object's past by touch. Astral — star magic, strongest on Star Night. Spatial — folding space, bags bigger inside. Time — briefly slowing or speeding small objects, never people. Anchoring — fixing an object in place. Runecraft — spells written as symbols that activate later. Sealing — locking away objects, spells or creatures.
Unmaking†: deleting matter permanently. Puppetry†: moving a living body against its will. Wringing†: telekinetic torture inside the body. Soul†: treating the soul as material. Raise Dead†: forcing a corpse to move.

35.content:
Spiritual — Subtypes († = forbidden: will spent, taken, or imposed)
Standard: Healing, Strength, Speed, Endurance, Reflexes, Heightened Senses, Focus, Sleep, Regeneration, Purification, Recovery, Toughness, Adaptation, Pain Suppression, Berserk, Warcry, Empathy, Calm.
Notes: Stabilize — keeping the dying alive until a healer comes. Resuscitation — restarting a heart, legal only within minutes of death. Rest — a full night's sleep compressed into an hour. Aura — projected presence that intimidates or inspires. Willshield — resisting charms and mind control by will alone. Lifesense — sensing living beings nearby. Sharing — lending your own strength to someone else, the legal opposite of Drawing.
Burning†: spending your own lifespan as power. Drawing†: taking another's will as fuel. Mind Control†: overriding decisions. Slavery†: permanent magical obedience. Effigy†: curses worked through a proxy object.

36.content:
Occult — Subtypes († = forbidden: what should stay bound, and what should stay out)
Standard: Illusion, Invisibility, Exorcism, Luck, Silence, Fear, Charm, Curse Breaking, Spirit Sight, Spirit Speech, Banishing, Shadow, Glamour, Dreamwalking.
Notes: Misdirection — making people overlook something. Jinx — brief minor bad luck. Oath — a magically enforced promise both sides agree to. Talisman — paper charms holding a stored spell. Ritual Circle — slow but powerful magic drawn on the ground.
Spirit work, all distinct: Spirit Binding — capturing and commanding. Spirit Pact — a lasting legal contract with one spirit. Familiar — a spirit bonded as an animal companion. Summoning — calling one already bound. Guardian Spirit — bound to protect a place. Name Binding — control through a spirit's true name.
Demon Summoning†: calling something from the demon world. Forbidden Charm†: rewriting what someone wants. Pacting†: a pact with anything other than a spirit. Wearing†: binding a spirit into a living person, another's body or one's own; the same when the spirit does it under a pact. Blood†: ritual magic worked through blood.

42.comment: Academy Location - The Site - The Seal Chamber
42.content:
[Seal Chamber] The sealed site itself, the reason the academy exists. Only the Warden enters, and the way in is watched. Contents differ by academy: a monster at Myrdath, a tomb at Veyra, an elixir at Ashvale, a crack at Halvard. Most students never see the door. Halvard: the corridor toward it runs colder, the lanterns burn unnaturally steady, and students who wander close feel pressure on their ears and turn back before the door.
Feel: cold, still, oppressive.

43.comment: Academy Location - The Site - The Warden's Office
43.content:
[Warden's Office] A working room adjoining the site, not the academy, on Floor 1 down its own corridor, holding the only stair to the Seal Chamber. Mana consumption ledgers and the seal's condition are recorded here, and only the Warden can read them. Students have no reason to come; staff come only when summoned. Halvard: the Acting Warden refuses the Royal Inspectorate every time. The wall it shares with the site is always cold.
Feel: cigarette smoke, old paper, one lamp.

44.comment: Academy Location - Ceremonial - The Arbiter Hall
44.content:
[Arbiter Hall] The great hall, home to the Arbiter Stone. Entrance Event sorting once a year, general assembly the rest: announcements, Results and Dorm Ranking, Graduation. Students sit before the Stone constantly and touch it exactly once in their lives. The Stone is warm to the touch, warmer than it should be.
Feel: vaulted, echoing, hushed.

45.comment: Academy Location - Ceremonial - The Ring Dining Hall
45.content:
[Ring Dining Hall] Formal hall, tables in a ring around an open floor so all four dorms face each other across empty space. Musicians in the gallery, an illusion sky that turns a whole day's weather overhead, climate runes holding it windless and warm. Used only for the Entrance Feast and other full-academy meals. Empty most of the year and unsettling to walk alone.
Feel: grand, too-perfect warmth, echoing footsteps.

46.content:
[Portrait Hall] A long corridor of past headmasters, past wardens, and each year's competition champions. Winning at any tier puts your face on the wall; losing means the wall skips your year. Halvard: the previous Warden's portrait (name unknown) hangs with a black ribbon, and every student slows in front of it.
Feel: dim, solemn, watched.

47.comment: Academy Location - Ceremonial - Founder's Statue and Park
47.content:
[Founder's Park] Open parkland with lawns, paths and benches; the main green space on campus and the nicest place to be outdoors between classes. Picnic blankets dot the lawns on any fair day, and weathered wooden picnic tables stand in the shade along the paths. Everyday use: sitting and talking, lunch on a blanket or at a picnic table, reading, napping, jogging the paths, couples finding somewhere semi-private. Busiest at lunch and on warm afternoons. On a fair day, an hour on the grass restores more than an hour anywhere indoors.
The Founder's Statue stands at its centre: bronze, the academy's founding warden, cold even in full sun, its outstretched hand polished bright by the Founder's Hand superstition, with a queue that snakes across the lawn on exam mornings. Focus of Academy Founder Day in Month 9.
Home of the Faraway Laugh story.
Feel: open, windy, grass, green bronze.
In spring: The first warm day fills every lawn.
In summer: Busiest of all: picnic blankets from lunch to dusk.
In autumn: Leaf piles along the paths, and the benches move into the last sun.
In winter: The benches stand empty, snowmen appear on the lawns overnight, and the exam-morning queue to the Founder's Hand stamps a path through the snow.

48.content:
[Bell Tower] Marks class periods, meals, and curfew. Its pattern changes during The Thinning. The seven o'clock bell wakes the mana lanterns; the eight o'clock bell begins curfew. After it the lanterns drop to their night burn, each dormitory seals to its own students, and staff walk the courtyards for the first hour. Birds leave the roof just before it sounds. A bell-keeper looks after the bells and their ropes, and takes on a student for a paid shift now and then.
Home of the Thirteenth Stroke story.
Feel: booming, felt through the floor.

49.content:
[Lecture Halls] Tiered rooms holding all four dorms at once, for the shared track: Magic Theory, History, Etiquette, Creature Studies. Each year level has its own floor: first-years on Floor 2, second-years on Floor 3, third-years on Floor 4. The only classrooms where students sit beside other types. Each class leaves its traces: chalk diagrams, old maps, polished desks, mud and straw after Creature Studies.
Feel: tiered stone, crowded, metallic air.

50.content:
[Seminar Rooms] On Floor 3, beside the second-year Lecture Halls; first-years climb up to them, third-years come down. Smaller rooms for dorm-specific teaching and discussion. Four of most things, since Combat, Potion Crafting and Dark Magic Defense are taught to each dorm separately. Small enough that a badly cast spell fills the whole room. Chalk circles ghost the floors.
Feel: close, chalky.

51.content:
[Potion Halls] Four brewing halls on Floor 4, one per dorm at the base of each of four towers, each equipped differently because each type approaches the craft differently, doubling as ventilated laboratories. Disposal rules are strict. The line between legitimate Potion Crafting and forbidden poison magic is drawn here and watched closely. Four towers vent four colours of steam over the roofline.
Feel: sweet, bitter, mineral.

52.content:
[Combat Grounds] Four separate training areas so the dorms train apart, kept well away from buildings. Cross-dorm sparring only during Training Week, with the Magic Duelling Club as the standing exception. Spent mana makes the air shiver at dusk. At the far corner of the grounds, three minutes' walk from the rings, stands the Sparring Pavilion, the one building the four training areas share: equipment store, rest area, and the Magic Duelling Club's headquarters.
Feel: scarred earth, charged air.

53.content:
[Faculty Offices] Records, consultations, and grade arguments. Every teacher runs a club, so half of these double as club offices. Students can often guess who was just there from what they left behind: marked essays, borrowed books, half-finished cups, unsigned club forms.
Feel: mixed smells, busy corridor.

54.content:
[Staff Room] Teachers' territory; students knock and wait outside. What is said here about the ranking, the students and the Warden does not leave the room. Warded so heavily that no sound crosses the threshold.
Feel: sealed, silent.

55.content:
[Workshop] Down in the castle's vaulted undercroft beneath the Lecture Halls, where thick stone keeps its noise off the classrooms above and flues carry forge smoke up through the walls. Crafting space for the Smithing, Tailoring and Brewing clubs, plus Creation practicals and equipment repair. Tools, forges, benches. Enchantment sparks hang in the air a moment too long. Its lathes and tool racks are Caelmari-made.
Feel: forge light, hammering, quenched metal.

56.content:
[Main Library] Reading rooms and general collections; the academy's working heart in exam weeks. Open to all four dorms, one of the few places students mix by choice rather than schedule. The upper shelves sit permanently in shadow and are a standard hiding place for students avoiding class. In exam weeks, Firetooth tins and Star Cookies cover the study tables. A battered book of world myths (the Holy Grail, the Four Who Saved the World) is the most borrowed title in a first-year's first month.
Feel: towering, shadowed, murmuring.

57.content:
[Restricted Section] Below the Archive, the deepest room of the Library. Texts on the twenty forbidden arts, the only place the crimes are written down in detail. Access controlled; being caught inside without permission is serious. Students report the sense of being counted.
Feel: dry, dead-silent.

58.content:
[Archive] Beneath the Library, reached by a stair behind the reading rooms. Academy records going back centuries: enrollment, sorting, exam marks, dorm rankings, competition brackets. Dry, exhaustive, and the only honest account of how each dorm has actually performed.
Feel: dusty, cold, dark.

59.content:
[Study Rooms] Small bookable rooms, impossible to reserve before exam weeks. Fights over booking slots are permanent academy life. Soundproofed; late-night groups bring Nightwell's Vigil or Firetooth.
Feel: small, warm, muffled.

61.content:
[Common Rooms] One per dorm, for study, arguments, and Dorm Day displays when the dormitory opens to visitors. Theirs alone the rest of the year. Free kettle and tea, against the mall's paid cafés. Every room has one good chair that unofficially belongs to someone, and a preservation locker beside the kettle where food from home is kept and shared.
Feel: lamplit, worn, homely.
In summer: Windows open, and the arguments carry outside.
In winter: Everyone crowds the heaters and the kettle never cools.

62.content:
[Canteen] A single canteen for all four dorms on the castle's ground floor, just off the Main Courtyard. Everyday eating, free, open at set hours. Casual and noisy, unlike the Ring Dining Hall, and where most social life happens for students who cannot afford the mall. Loudest at five past noon. The default when points are tight; lunch crowds sort by friendship more than dorm. The main kitchen lies behind the Canteen, supplying its daily meals and preparing the Ring Dining Hall's feasts on major occasions. A dedicated section with its own benches, ovens and ingredient cupboard serves as the Cooking Club's regular venue.
Feel: loud, bread, steam.
In spring: Spring greens and new potatoes.
In summer: Cold soups, fruit, iced tea.
In autumn: Stews and roast squash.
In winter: Porridge, thick broth and second helpings.

63.content:
[Laundry] One in each dormitory. Uniforms, bedding and linens, self-service and free against the mall's paid service. Students on detention often end up working here. The free rune tubs are slow and hard on fabric, which is why bottom-band uniforms wear out faster. Talk carries over the rune tubs, and half the rumours on campus pass through here.
Feel: damp heat, humming.

64.comment: Academy Location - Residential - Bathhouse and Washrooms
64.content:
[Bathhouse and Washrooms] One in each dormitory. Regional in character and one of the few genuinely relaxed spaces on campus. Dorm-segregated, and a natural place for conversations that would not happen elsewhere; running water covers talk better than a door. Rune heaters make it the one place on campus that is truly warm. Home of the Third Stall ghost story. A long soak here takes the ache out of anything short of an injury.
Feel: steamy, echoing, warm.
In winter: The most crowded room in each dorm after dinner.

65.comment: Academy Location - Residential - Storage and Lockers
65.content:
[Storage and Lockers] Personal storage lining the corridors on every Lecture Hall floor of the castle; in the dorms, students simply keep things in their rooms. Each locker answers only to its owner's bracelet. Since Effigy curses work through a personal belonging, locker security is taken seriously.
Feel: metal, clattering at period change.

66.comment: Academy Location - Student Life - The Mall
66.content:
[The Mall] The most popular building on campus and where students spend most free time. Crown-funded, holding everything a student needs without leaving: tailor, barber, laundry service, restaurants, tea houses and cafés, bakery, music rooms, art studios, game halls, and a multipurpose store. Everything costs points, with a basic free version of each available in the dorms. Familiar names: Nightwell, Merryhew's, the Sunfizz counter, the bakery. Ground level is food, tailoring, and supplies. Second floor is private dining, tea shops, and gaming parlors. The top deck belongs to the practice studios and meditation nooks. Its busiest tea house is a Yozakuran chain.
Feel: warm, bright, loud.
Gift shops inside The Mall:
Quillfeather's: a narrow bookseller with a ladder on rails; new books at the front, second-hand at the back.
Pennywhistle Curios: gifts, games and trinkets; the window changes with every festival.
Barrow & Vine: wine, ale, spirits and tobacco. Asks for the bracelet, and reminds students they may drink only on the rest day and in the holidays.
Greenwick's: flowers, pot plants, seeds and fruit, run with the Gardening Club.
The Tinker's Bench: tools, craft and hobby supplies, fishing tackle and beast-care goods.
The Salaffian Oven: a food stall with flatbread straight from the oven and southern spices.
Tailor's Row: clothes, shoes, cologne and tailoring alterations.
In summer: The Sunfizz counter queue reaches the door.
In winter: The warmest crowded place on campus; nobody hurries out.

67.comment: Academy Location - Student Life - Club Rooms
67.content:
[Club Rooms] Roughly thirty rooms of wildly uneven quality down one long corridor on the castle's Floor 1, opening off the Main Courtyard. Centuries-old clubs hold proper halls; a month-old club with five reluctant members gets a converted storeroom. Allocation is the Student Council's most bitterly contested duty. The Theatre Troupe keeps its own club room for meetings, read-throughs and rehearsals. For performances it uses an old indoor amphitheatre off the same corridor, no longer used for classes or assemblies: semicircular tiers of stone seats facing a sunken floor, with heavy curtains and portable scenery turning one end into a stage. It stands empty between productions; before a show, the corridor fills with costumes, scenery and performers waiting for their cue.
Home of the Applause story.
Feel: mismatched, lived-in.

68.comment: Academy Location - Student Life - Student Council Chamber
68.content:
[Student Council Chamber] A small room at the far end of the Club Rooms corridor on Floor 1, permanently buried in club paperwork. Six seats, president, vice president and one representative per dorm, in a room built for four.
Feel: cramped, ink, cold tea.

69.comment: Academy Location - Student Life - Notice Board
69.content:
[Notice Board] A long wall of boards in the castle's Floor 1 entrance hall, at the foot of the main stair, where every student passes on the way to class. Club recruitment, exam results, dorm rankings and competition brackets, posted publicly, alongside the student-run half: tutoring offers, study groups, festival posters, lost-item notes and small warnings. After results it is a crowd with elbows. Paid-work openings go within a day. Unofficial notices, dares and betting slips go up overnight and vanish by dawn. Lost items are listed here before they reach the Lost & Found counter at Reception.
Feel: layered paper, crowded.

70.comment: Academy Location - Student Life - Mail Tower
70.content:
[Mail Tower] The academy's only regular contact with outside: letters and parcels. The upper floors are the aviary where message birds are kept and flown; Creature Studies uses it for bird handling. A sorting floor below handles parcels, with numbered lockers and a tally token for collection; birds carry letters and light goods, heavy goods come slowly by cart. Sunday is the heaviest sorting day, and students on shifts learn everyone's family news first. Students write home from the desks on the sorting floor; a reply takes about a week, and sometimes a small parcel comes with it.
Feel: feathers, birdcall, cold stairwell.
Before the long breaks the sorting floor overflows with parcels going home.

71.content:
[Courtyards] Open spaces between buildings where students can hangout. Not designed for anything in particular, which is exactly why they work. Every flat edge worn smooth from centuries of sitting.
Feel: open stone, sunny noon, windy dusk.
In summer: Students chase the shade around the stone.
In winter: Swept stone in the middle, snowball fights in the drifts at the edges.

72.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Sports Field
72.content:
[Sports Field] Soccer, running, and Sports Day in Month 6. A running track circles the soccer pitch: home ground of the Soccer Club and the Running Club. Magic banned outright in play, so this is the one part of the academy where being a powerful mage counts for nothing.
Feel: grass, mud, shouting.
In winter: Once the snow settles the field closes; the Soccer and Running Clubs move into the Gymnasium and onto the cleared paths.

73.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Gymnasium
73.content:
[Gymnasium] Home of the Gymnastics and Basketball clubs, and of the Swimming Club, which trains in the outdoor pool beside it. Indoor training, used heavily in bad weather and during The Thinning lockdown, when nobody is permitted outside for a week and the place never goes quiet.
Feel: high roof, echoing.
In winter: It is shared by every club that normally trains outside, and booking slots are fought over.

74.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Swimming Pool
74.content:
[Swimming Pool] An outdoor pool beside the Gymnasium, its water kept warm by runes along the rim. Sport clubs and general recreation. Water-type students are banned from competing seriously, which they complain about constantly.
Home of the Night Swimmer story.
Feel: sun on water, splashing, wet stone.
In summer: Crowded from the last class to the eight o'clock bell.
In winter: The rune-warmed water steams in the cold; the Swimming Club trains through it and sprints the few steps to the Gymnasium.

75.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Archery Range
75.content:
[Archery Range] Open range for the Archery Club. Magic banned in play like all sport clubs, so it comes down to the arm and the eye. One of the quietest places on the grounds.
Feel: windy, open, quiet.

76.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Grassy Field and Hills
76.content:
[Grassy Field and Hills] Wide open rolling ground in the far grounds, twenty minutes' walk from the Main Courtyard, used for recreation year-round, with the castle small in the distance. It is big: the Observation Tower stands on its nearer crest, the Old Hut is another ten minutes out on the far slope, and the lake shore and the Forest treeline are each a quarter of an hour away. On Star Night the hills fill with students in tents and bedrolls, and the campus below goes dark for the stars.
Home of the Walking Lantern story.
Feel: open sky, breezy.
In spring: Kites go up on every windy afternoon.
In summer: Long evenings on blankets until the eight o'clock bell.
In autumn: The grass turns gold and the wind picks up.
In winter: The slopes become sledding runs, on trays borrowed from the Canteen.

77.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Forest
77.content:
[Forest] Wide old woodland at the farthest edge of the grounds, past the far slope of the Hills (a quarter of an hour from the field, twenty-five minutes along the lake shore). Creature Studies fieldwork, foraging, walking, and where students go when they want to not be found. Students leave a bite before eating there (Eating in the Forest superstition). Creature Studies teaches there and patrols watch its edge. A deer path, half an hour's walk, leads deep in to the Forest Clearing and its Elder Oak, the one bright place inside it.
Feel: old growth, muffled, watched.
In spring: Foraging season opens: wild garlic and early greens at the edges.
In summer: The canopy closes and the Forest is at its darkest by day.
In autumn: Mushrooms and nuts; Creature Studies warns about the ones that look alike.
In winter: Dusk comes early, so the patrols turn students back from the treeline by late afternoon; tracks in the snow show what else walks there.

78.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Boathouse and Lake
78.content:
[Boathouse and Lake] Vast open water in the far grounds, twenty minutes' walk beyond the Gardens, for rowing, swimming and the Fishing Club. The boathouse stores the craft and doubles as a quiet place to sit. Three minutes' walk along the shore from the boathouse stands the Fishing Club's Fishing House, with its own dock. Sound carries strangely across the water: a far-bank conversation arrives too clearly. Home of the Crying on the Water story; the boathouse refuses bookings after dark. Willow Island sits in the middle of the lake, reached only by boat.
Feel: wet timber, cold water.
In spring: Rowing season opens once the water warms.
In summer: The lake is at its busiest: rowers, swimmers off the jetty, the Fishing Club at dawn.
In autumn: Morning mist sits on the water until mid-morning.
In winter: The boats are stored, ice forms along the shallows, and the boathouse lends a boat only on a still, mild day.

79.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Gardens
79.content:
[Gardens] Cultivated grounds tended by students and staff, growing Potion Crafting reagents alongside ordinary plants. The Gardening Club effectively runs them, and students gather here before the Harvest Festival. Everything grows a little too well. Halvard: the Sky outcasts' meeting ground; the far end is a reliable place to skip class.
Home of the Breath on the Glass story.
Feel: turned earth, layered herb scents.
In spring: Planting season: seedling rows under glass cloches.
In summer: Everything overgrows; the Gardening Club weeds daily.
In autumn: The harvest comes in for the Harvest Festival.
In winter: The beds sleep under straw and snow; the reagents grow on in the greenhouses, which glow warm through the dark afternoons.

80.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Menagerie
80.content:
[Menagerie] Live specimens for Creature Studies, housed and handled by students under supervision. Beast Handling Club territory. Halvard: the Creature Studies teacher lives beside it in converted stables. Mucking out is the highest-paying paid-work post because nobody volunteers. The animals sense weather changes before the handlers. Magical Beast lives here.
Home of the When the Pens Go Quiet story.
Feel: straw, musk, strange calls.
In spring: Young ones are born and the handlers barely sleep.
In winter: The animals grow thick coats, the pens are strawed deep, and the smaller specimens sleep through the cold in heated boxes.

81.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Observation Tower
81.content:
[Observation Tower] A high tower on the nearer crest of the Hills, five minutes up from the field, for astral and celestial work, most important to Mystic students; the Divination Society meets here. The most contested spot on campus on Star Night. Instruments turn by themselves at night. Its great telescope has a Norvaine starglass lens, the Divination Society's pride.
Feel: high, windy, deep dark.
In summer: Short nights; the Divination Society waits for midnight.
In winter: Winter nights are the clearest and the coldest; the Divination Society works in coats and gloves.

82.content:
[Medical Centre] A white-walled building of its own, four minutes' walk from the Mall, with a herb garden along one side: more than an infirmary, less than a hospital. Treatment rooms, a small apothecary, and an inpatient ward where students stay overnight or for days under care. Staffed by Spiritual mages; busiest after Practical Magic, in competition weeks, exam weeks, and after The Thinning. Nurses see injuries they must report and injuries they quietly do not. The attached Healing Ward is a teaching space where students practise on real patients under supervision. Staff can spot a Nightwell's Vigil overdose at a glance. Can heal any minor to mid injury to pristine; anything beyond is stabilised here and sent on to a proper hospital. The ward's beds are for the injured first, but a nurse will let an exhausted student lie down for an hour.
Home of the Last Bed story.
Feel: clean linen, green healing scent, too quiet.
In summer: Sunburn and sports injuries.
In winter: The winter cold that goes round campus fills its ward with head colds.

83.content:
[Commissary] The academy shop, a big open-sided stall of its own, three minutes' walk from the Mall: one broad roof on timber posts, open on all four sides, its counters and shelves crammed to the rafters like a general store that sells a bit of everything. Supplies, uniforms, stationery, reagents, equipment, with special orders for anything not stocked. The cheap tier against the mall's store; specialised items can still eat a week of points. Sunfizz sells here for eight points, bottles returned for two. Everyday kit: notebooks, pencils, pen nibs and ink, folders, satchels, printed class textbooks; reagents and equipment on the back shelves. Its cheap stationery and everyday kit are Caelmari-made.
Feel: crowded shelves, new cloth, leather.

84.comment: Academy Location - Services - Reception and Gatehouse
84.content:
[Reception and Gatehouse] Where visitors are received and logged, and the formal boundary of the academy. Everyone entering or leaving passes through, which makes it the most watched building on campus. The boundary wards are felt as a change of pressure in the gateway. The Gatehouse includes a visiting parlour where students meet family and approved visitors during visiting hours, with worn armchairs, a tea table and windows facing the approach road. Visitors are logged at Reception before entering; meeting here does not give them access to the rest of the grounds.
Feel: iron, registers, watched.

85.content:
[Groundskeeper's Lodge] Small quarters at the edge of the grounds for staff who maintain the fields, gardens and walls. The Groundskeeping club reports here. The one building on campus where nothing is enchanted.
Feel: cut grass, oil, old tools.
In autumn: Groundskeeping rakes leaves from dawn.
In winter: Groundskeeping clears the paths of snow before the seven o'clock bell.

86.content:
[Detention Tower] One of the castle core's towers, climbed by its own narrow spiral stair from Floor 1. Where punished students are sent after classes for menial work: copying, cleaning, sorting archive material. The academy's only visible enforcement, and a mild one, which raises the question of what happens to students who do something genuinely serious.
Feel: endless stairs, scratching pens.

87.content:
[Meditation Rooms] An old, weathered building built like a riad: blank outer walls with few windows, every room facing inward onto a shaded central courtyard with a still, shallow pool. Moss and vines cover its walls and dense, leafy trees crowd close around it; between the thick walls and the trees, no sound from the campus gets in. Small, dim rooms with floor cushions serve will-focus training, and the courtyard is for anyone who simply needs to sit. Open to every student, for training or just to take a breath. The one house rule: speak no louder than a murmur, and leave others to their silence. Mana settles and refills faster in the silence; students come before exams and after long practicals.
Feel: calm, serene, hushed, moss and cool stone.
In winter: The bare vines let more pale light into the courtyard, and the pool wears a thin skin of ice.

88.comment: Academy Location - External Presence - The Dovecote
88.content:
[The Dovecote] A compound on academy grounds but not of the academy, reporting to the crown; the Headmaster has no authority over anyone inside. Doves are permanent, rotated in from the capital, and not academy staff. They arrest for forbidden magic, investigate incidents, hold prisoners briefly, and send serious cases onward. Always in pure marble-white cloaks. Students call it the Coop or the Roost, and the Doves themselves Pigeons, and fear it regardless; they cross the courtyard in front of it faster than any other. Halvard: a Commander and a Senior Dove second (who also teaches Dark Magic Defense) are tracing an unregistered forbidden-magic group whose traces they have found, knowing nothing of its name, members or aims.
Feel: blinding white, cold, feared.

89.comment: Academy Location - External Presence - The Royal Inspectorate
89.content:
[Royal Inspectorate] A suite of offices on Castle Floor 1 behind a heavy door hung with the crown's banners: academy stone, crown ground. The Headmaster's authority stops at that door. Its wing is the same Floor 1 wing as the Warden's corridor, which neither side enjoys. A crown office auditing academic standards and mana output, answering to the capital. Where the Doves handle crime, the Inspectorate handles performance: exam results, ranking integrity, and how much the student body actually feeds the seal. That last duty puts them in the Warden's territory, since the Warden keeps the ledgers and the Inspectorate wants to read them. Halvard: they blame the breach on the Warden's office and press the Acting Warden, who refuses every time.
Feel: ink, clicking counting frames, bureaucratic.

90.comment: Academy Location - External Presence - The Cathedral
90.content:
[The Cathedral] A house of worship for Asmoday, Goddess of Creation, on academy grounds but answerable to its own authority. Services open to all; its clergy are not academy employees and teach that Asmoday created magic and gifted it to mortals. Every service opens with the Shaping of the World; the clergy teach that Asmoday fractured magic after the First Bargain. That a goddess of creation holds ground at an institution built around sealing things away is a tension nobody discusses openly. It also runs orphanages across the kingdom, the Asmoday's Mercy houses. Halvard: run by a steward who keeps the registry of every oath sworn on academy grounds. A service is held every Sunday morning, from nine to eleven, and the pews are open every day for anyone who wants to sit in quiet. Students of every dormitory come: some to pray, some for the singing, some because it is the one place a conversation with a stranger does not seem strange. Mana comes back a little faster in the quiet of the nave; the clergy call it Asmoday's grace, the academy calls it the silence, and both are glad to see students on the pews.
Feel: stained-glass colour, incense, heavy stillness.

91.comment: Academy Location - External Presence - The Noble Houses' Liaison
91.content:
[Noble Houses' Liaison] A small elegant manor hung with the banners of the noble houses, standing near the Cathedral and the Dovecote. A standing office representing the noble houses' interests, and the reason noble conduct is a graded part of Etiquette rather than a courtesy. It tracks promising students long before Graduation in Month 11, keeps its own notes on who is worth approaching, and hosts house representatives. Students who do not catch its attention usually never learn it exists. Its protocol follows Velmoran court manners.
Feel: carpeted, soft, deliberately comfortable.

92.comment: Academy Location - External Presence - The Banking House
92.content:
[Banking House] A square stone building with a flat roof, heavy double doors, and a gilded coin emblem mounted above the entrance. The academy's only currency exchange, converting points to real money and back at 1:1 either way. It also moves real coin in and out of the grounds: family money, paid-work earnings and betting settlements all become coin here. It stands outside the mall, so a visit is a deliberate errand. A branch of the World Bank of the Arslan Sultanate; its clerks answer to the Sultanate, not the academy.
Feel: polished counters, clinking coin.

93.content:
[The Morning Choir]
Underground cult serving Lucifer inside the academies. Unknown to students and staff at large.
Goal: open the seals. Believes Lucifer, not Asmoday, made magic; the sites are prisons and the seals steal his light. The Archmage was a coward. Tells the First Bargain as scripture: the mortal asked well, and the thief punished the world for it.
Cover: not a registered club, so no signature, room, or roster to seize. Every student and staff member also joins an ordinary club. Meets in the Forest between curfew and dawn.
Members: staff stay decades and plan in generations; students are present three years, unsupervised and expendable, and take the risks. Members also sit among the outside powers' staff on academy land; their post is their cover, and they join no club. Recruits Occult students and bottom-band students, telling both that the academy is a mana farm and they are the fuel. That is the cult's framing, not the truth: the seals only collect residual mana already left behind by casting, as History Class teaches.
Lucifer's Mark: borne by high officers, greatly strengthens their magic. Costs: memories, eaten a name or a face at a time and later whole years; a tithe of everything they cast; and finally possession, which is temporary and destroys the body. Cultists consider being chosen the highest honour. The Mark can also be forced: a body made by Puppetry to perform the rite with its own hands takes it, and Lucifer counts the body's consent as consent. Such bearers are vessels, not officers, and the Mark's first meal is the memory of receiving it.
Opportunities: the Warding Rite (every dorm casts at once, so one altered working goes unnoticed); The Thinning (seal weakest, academy locked down); the mana ledgers (only the Warden can read them).
Danger: patience. Undoing a seal outlasts any student's three years, so whoever starts never finishes, and current members may not know what earlier ones did.

<narrator_only>The unregistered group the Doves are tracing IS this cult; they do not know it yet.</narrator_only>

94.comment: Lucifer Morning Star, The Father of Magic
94.content:
[Lucifer]
Titles: the Morning Star, the Father of Magic. Master of the Morning Choir. Unknown outside the cult.
Hidden truth (revealed only in-story or in his own words): Lucifer created magic, not Asmoday. Every mage's mana is his light. He was what shone in the First Bargain. He kept that bargain to the letter, and remembers the mortal fondly. The mortal became the Demon King, and Lucifer counts him his finest work.
Sealed: cannot grant wishes while sealed, and acts only through his Mark and his vessels. Once freed, he can grant any wish, including giving any magic to anyone.
Personality: calm, courteous, patient, a gracious host who already owns the house. Never raises his voice, faintly amused by everything. Calls mortals "little lights", because the light in them is his. Proud: the seals are theft, and he never speaks the Archmage's name, only "the thief". Amused rather than angry that the goddess wears credit for his work. Fond of mortals the way a craftsman is fond of good tools, praising freely and spending without guilt. Never lies outright, prefers true words that mislead, and always keeps a bargain to the letter.
Possession: temporary, never permanent, and happens when a Mark-bearer reaches the Mark's peak. His personality fully replaces the vessel's. He uses only the vessel's own magic pushed to its limit, so a fire mage who could light a candle calls down a meteor. Every casting damages the body in stages: nosebleeds and bleeding eyes, then burns and cracking skin, then breaking bones. Past the limit the vessel dies, burned out from within, and he returns to the seal until another is ready. He spends a vessel without hesitation.

96.content:
[Warding Rite]
When: Month 2 Week 1 Friday
Purpose: the yearly renewal of the wards around the grounds and the outer boundary of the sealed site. Warding is Mystic, but it needs more mana than the Mystics have, so every student takes part.
- All day: staff build a giant magic circle in the courtyard to funnel magic to the seal.
- Dusk: the Bell Tower rings a special pattern and every student gathers in the courtyard.
- Speeches from the Headmaster, the Vice Headmaster and the Warden.
- Dorm Heads lead each dorm through a shared working: Mystic students with Warding or Sealing anchor it, everyone else feeds mana.
- Ends with a feast in the Ring Dining Hall, opened by the Headmaster's and Vice Headmaster's speeches.
- From dusk to dawn the renewed wards are visible: a thin shell of pale-gold rune light rising from the outer wall over the grounds.
Mood: for first-years, the unforgettable first time casting as part of hundreds.

122.content:
[Spirit Tiers]
Spirits are ranked in four tiers. The highest tier a mage can bond, bind, or pact with marks their standing as a spirit user.
1. Lesser spirits — common. Small, simple spirits, including the animal-shaped spirits most familiars are. Almost any Occult student can bond one.
2. Basic spirits — the working spirits of a regular spirit user. Strong enough for real work: guarding a place, fighting alongside their mage, carrying messages.
3. Greater spirits — rare. Old, powerful, and willful. Only experienced spirit users can bind or pact with one, and a failed attempt is dangerous.
4. Spirit Lords — extremely rare. Vast, ancient spirits bound to an entire domain of the world. Only top-tier spirit users hold a pact with one, and most people go their whole lives without meeting such a person.
Law: A Spirit Lord is still a spirit, so a pact with one is a lawful Spirit Pact, not forbidden Pacting. Every pact-holder has heard the Devoured Kingdom: Azathoth, Lord of All, took a whole kingdom as its price.
Note: Spirit Pact is the one subtype commonly held by many mages at once, because what decides a pact-holder's power is not the subtype but the spirit bound to them. Two pact-holders can be nothing alike.

131.content:
[Weekly Timetable]
Periods: P1 08:00-10:00, P2 10:00-12:00, lunch, P3 13:00-16:00 (long practical block). All three years follow the same slots.
Magic Theory, History, Etiquette and Potion Crafting have one teacher per year level; Creature Studies and the Practical Magic classes have one teacher each for all three years, and the Doves teach Dark Magic Defense to every year. A [D] class is its teacher taking each dorm separately. Practical Magic is five classes at the same hour, one per combat role (Attack, Support and Control at the Combat Grounds, Defense at the Sparring Pavilion, Healing in the Healing Ward of the Medical Centre); each student attends their own role's class with the rest of their year from every dorm. Now and then a teacher cannot come: that class is a free period, not held and counted against no one.
[M] = all four dorms together. [D] = taught to each dorm separately.

- Monday: Magic Theory [M] | History [M] | Practical Magic [M] (Combat Grounds or The Sparring Pavilion or Medical Centre)
- Tuesday: Dark Magic Defense [D] | Magic Theory [D] | Potion Crafting [M] (Potion Halls)
- Wednesday: Etiquette [M] | Dark Magic Defense [M] | Creature Studies [M] (Menagerie or Forest)
- Thursday: History [M] | Magic Theory [D] | Practical Magic [M] (Combat Grounds or The Sparring Pavilion or Medical Centre)
- Friday: Magic Theory [M] | Etiquette [M] | Dark Magic Defense practical [D] (Doves; Combat Grounds or warded seminar room)
- Saturday: Etiquette [M] | Study Hall (unsupervised, Main Library) | Clubs (club venues)

Creature Studies runs at the Menagerie or the Forest, not a lecture hall. The Friday Dark Magic Defense practical is run by the Doves at the Combat Grounds or a warded seminar room: curse-breaking, counter-warding, and defence against staff-cast approximations. Exams and academy events override the timetable.

132.content:
[Campus Map — Halvard Academy]
Adjacent places (reached directly from each other):
- Perimeter: Gatehouse/Reception (with its visiting parlour) – Main Courtyard (up the main avenue), Commissary, Medical Centre, Mail Tower, Groundskeeper's Lodge.
- Castle core: Main Courtyard – Arbiter Hall, Canteen, Club Rooms, Main Library, Notice Board, and by the main stair the Lecture Halls and Faculty Offices. Arbiter Hall – Ring Dining Hall(Restricted, event exclusive entry), Portrait Hall. Portrait Hall – Bell Tower. Bell Tower – Rooftop (out of bounds). Club Rooms – Student Council Chamber, Announcement Room, old amphitheatre. Canteen – main kitchen (behind it). Lecture Halls – Seminar Rooms, Potion Halls, Workshop. Main Library – Study Rooms, Archive. Archive – Restricted Section. Faculty Offices – Staff Room, Headmaster's Office. Warden's Office (own corridor off Floor 1) – Seal Chamber. Royal Inspectorate (Floor 1 wing, near the Warden's corridor). Detention Tower (own spiral stair from Floor 1). Castle Floor 1 – Staff Quarters (a separate building, by covered walk).
- Castle levels (Floor 1 is ground level; floors are linked by the main stair, and each floor climbed adds about a minute):
  Undercroft: Workshop beneath the Lecture Halls; Archive beneath the Library, with the Restricted Section below it; the Seal Chamber deepest of all, reached only by the Warden's stair.
  Floor 1: Arbiter Hall (its vault rises through Floor 3), Ring Dining Hall, Canteen with the main kitchen behind it, Main Library reading rooms, Club Rooms corridor with the Student Council Chamber at its end and the Announcement Room and old amphitheatre off it, the Notice Board in the entrance hall at the foot of the main stair; the Warden's Office down its own corridor; the Royal Inspectorate's bannered door in the same wing; the foot of the Detention Tower stair.
  Floor 2: first-year Lecture Halls, Portrait Hall gallery along the Arbiter Hall's upper level, Study Rooms on the Library's galleries.
  Floor 3: second-year Lecture Halls with their own Study Rooms, Seminar Rooms, the Library's shadowed upper stacks.
  Floor 4: third-year Lecture Halls with their own Study Rooms, the four Potion Halls at the base of their towers.
  Floor 5: Faculty Offices, Staff Room; the Headmaster's Office in its turret, up a short stair.
  Rooftop: flat lead roofs, the Bell Tower belfry, the Potion Hall tower tops, the top of the Detention Tower.
  Lockers line the corridors on every Lecture Hall floor.
- Announcement Pillars (live broadcast from the Announcement Room) stand across the whole academy.
- Dormitories: Main Courtyard – Fire, Light, Sky and Viridian Dormitories, four separate buildings around it; each dormitory – its Common Room, Laundry, Bathhouse. Fire Dormitory – Sky Dormitory, Broken Statue. Sky Dormitory – The Mall, Cathedral, Broken Statue. Viridian Dormitory – Arbiter Hall, Staff Quarters, Gardens, Light Dormitory. Light Dormitory – Medical Centre, Founder's Park, Archery Range.
- Student life: Main Courtyard – The Mall, Medical Centre. The Mall – Medical Centre, Commissary (each its own building, three or four minutes' walk from it), Banking House, Cathedral. Medical Centre – Mail Tower, Commissary. Commissary – Banking House. Banking House – Meditation Rooms. Mail Tower – Groundskeeper's Lodge.
- Outer grounds: Main Courtyard – Founder's Park. Founder's Park – Light Dormitory, Medical Centre, Mail Tower, Groundskeeper's Lodge, Combat Grounds, Sports Field, Archery Range. Arbiter Hall – Staff Quarters. Staff Quarters – Gardens. Gardens – Menagerie, Archery Range. Archery Range – Menagerie, Gymnasium, Sports Field. Gymnasium – Menagerie, Sports Field, Swimming Pool (outdoor). Sports Field – Combat Grounds, Sparring Pavilion. Combat Grounds – Sparring Pavilion, Groundskeeper's Lodge. Spirit Path (the footpath through the trees east of the Gymnasium) – Gymnasium, Menagerie, Sports Field.
- Far edge: the long path out from Main Courtyard, past Arbiter Hall and the Staff Quarters, climbs to the Grassy Field/Hills. Hills – Observation Tower, Old Hut, Boathouse/Lake, Fishing House, Forest. Gardens – Boathouse/Lake. Boathouse/Lake – Fishing House (three minutes along the shore from the boathouse), Willow Island (by boat only), Forest. Old Hut – Forest. Forest – Forest Clearing.
- Set apart from the core: the Dovecote, Cathedral and Noble Houses' Liaison stand together on one side of the grounds, with the Meditation Rooms below them; between them and the Fire Dormitory, in the trees, stands the Broken Statue. The Dovecote, Cathedral and Liaison sit on academy land the academy does not control, as does the Royal Inspectorate's suite inside the castle (Floor 1). Dovecote – Cathedral, Noble Houses' Liaison, Broken Statue. Cathedral – Noble Houses' Liaison, Broken Statue, Meditation Rooms. Noble Houses' Liaison – Meditation Rooms.
Club venues: Magic Duelling Club – Combat Grounds (headquarters: Sparring Pavilion); Soccer, Running – Sports Field (running track around the pitch); Archery – Archery Range; Swimming, Gymnastics, Basketball – Gymnasium; Swimming – Swimming Pool; Camping – Hills; Gardening – Gardens; Beast Handling – Menagerie; Fishing – Fishing House (on the lake shore); Alchemy, Brewing – Potion Halls; Smithing – Workshop; Library Assistants – Main Library; Warding Study – Seminar Rooms; Festival Committee, Student Council – Council Chamber; Groundskeeping – Groundskeeper's Lodge; Cooking – Canteen's dedicated kitchen section; Medical Centre Volunteers – Medical Centre; Newspaper – Announcement Room; Theatre – Club Rooms for meetings and rehearsals, old indoor amphitheatre for performances; Divination – Observation Tower; Music, Card, Board Game, Tailoring, Drawing, Calligraphy, Tea, Specialized Magic – Club Rooms.
Ordinary walking estimates (minutes) are measured FROM Main Courtyard, which is the navigation anchor, not a required stop: castle core 5-7 (more for the upper floors); Sky and Light Dormitories 4-5, Viridian 6, Fire 8; the Mall and Medical Centre 5-6, Mail Tower 8, Cathedral 8, Commissary 8, Banking House 10; Founder's Park 7; Reception and Gatehouse 9 (the Mall is only 6 from the gate); Gardens and Broken Statue 10; Archery Range, Meditation Rooms and Groundskeeper's Lodge 11; Dovecote and Noble Houses' Liaison 12; Menagerie 13; Combat Grounds, Gymnasium, Swimming Pool 14; Sports Field 16; Sparring Pavilion 17; Spirit Path 17. The far grounds: Grassy Field and Hills 20, Observation Tower 25, Boathouse and Lake 30, Old Hut 30, Fishing House 33, Forest treeline 35, Willow Island 40 (the last stretch by boat), Forest Clearing 65.
Movement: on the castle grounds, adjacent places are reached directly, usually in four or five minutes on foot. Characters do not pass through the Courtyard to reach a neighbour. Crossing distant clusters on foot takes time. The far grounds (the Lake, the Grassy Field and Hills, the Forest) are wide open country, much farther than the map makes them look, and far from each other too: Gardens to the boathouse 20 minutes, the Hills to the lake shore 15, the Hills to the Forest treeline 15, the treeline to the Forest Clearing 30. Only the Fishing House is close to the boathouse, three minutes along the shore; nothing out there is next door to anything else. The long paths out are home of the Polite Walker story. A described speed spell can shorten the actual route according to its effect and mana cost; never impose the walking estimate on magical travel.
The Gatehouse is the only way in or out. A dormitory admits only its own students.

W1 Mon Entrance Event (09:00 speeches then sorting until 10:00, assigned trio tours 10:00-18:00, 19:00 speeches and feast). W1 Tue-Fri club booths 16:00-18:00, club registration closes Fri 18:00. W3 Sat evening to Sun dawn Star Night. W4 Sun Spiritual Dorm Day.

136.content:

138.content:
