W1 Mon-Thu End of Semester exams. W2 Fri Results & Dorm Ranking. W3 open. W4 Mid-Year Break, students go home.

139.content:
[Current month: Month 6]
W1 Mon-Fri Return Week. W3 Sat Sports Day (magic banned outright). W4 Wed-Sat Academy Competition (cross-dorm teams of 4).

140.content:
[Current month: Month 7]
W2 Magical & Science Fair. W3 Mon-Sun The Thinning: the seal is at its weakest, the academy is locked down for the week, nobody outside.

141.content:
[Current month: Month 8]
W2 Thu evening to Sun Traveling Circus visits. W3 Thu-Sat Academy Showcase. W4 Sun Elemental Dorm Day.

142.content:
[Current month: Month 9]
W1 Mon-Thu Midterm. W2 Thu-Sat Academy Bazaar. W3 Sat Academy Founder Day. W4 Wed-Sat Kingdom Competition at the Royal Arena in Avalon, the capital (four academies, one team each; only the teams travel, Halvard's with Gavlan Haverton: they fly out Tue and home Sun).

143.content:
[Current month: Month 10]
W1 Tue Remembrance Day. W2 Sun Occult Dorm Day. W3 Mon-Thu Student Council election campaign; W3 Fri 16:00-18:00 debate in the Seminar Rooms; W3 Sat 13:00-16:00 voting in the Main Courtyard replaces clubs, with results after counting. W4 Fri evening to Sun Harvest Festival.

144.content:
[Current month: Month 11]
W1 Mon-Thu End of Semester exams; no classes from W1 Fri until Graduation. W1 Sat Results & Final Ranking. W2 Mon-Sat Academy Trip (Sunreach Bay, abroad; a full day by airship each way: out Mon, home Sat). W3 Mon to W4 Mon World Competition, abroad (the national four). W4 Sun Graduation (third-years leave the next morning).

145.content:
[Current month: Month 12]
Kingdom-wide holiday all month, students go home, campus nearly empty.

201.content:
[Period Change]
Rule: when the bell ends a period, the main corridors are impassable for four minutes, then empty as fast as they filled.
Lateness: teachers time the Lecture Halls to Seminar Rooms walk to the minute; no excuse works.
Feel: crushing, deafening.

202.content:
[Skipping Class]
Spots: the boathouse, the far end of the Gardens, the dark upper stacks of the Main Library, the stairwells behind the Workshop.
Forest: the only real disappearance, so staff check it first.
Risk: an hour missing gets a slow walk to the Medical Centre; an afternoon means the hills, visible from the Bell Tower.

203.content:
[Exam Week]
Signs: the Main Library stays full at night; Study Rooms unbookable a fortnight ahead; the canteen serves whoever turns up whenever; daily mana exhaustion in the Medical Centre; Firetooth and Nightwell's Vigil as study currency; Star Cookies sold out before seven; Dragonchess boards gather dust.
Mood: everyone short with everyone, forgiven afterwards.

204.content:
[Assignments and Group Work]
Load: Magic Theory sets weekly written work; History sets essays nobody starts early; Creature Studies and Potion Crafting set assigned pair practicals, so students from different dorms end up owing each other favours; Combat sets no homework and everyone points it out.
Group work: the standard excuse for being anywhere at any hour; staff know how often it is true. Library tables and club rooms become meeting points near exams.

205.content:
[The Third Stall]
Where: one stall in every Bathhouse and Washroom block, always occupied, never answers.
Rule: knock twice and something knocks back; knock a third time and the latch opens on an empty stall. Never test it after the night bell.
Passed down as a senior's joke.

206.content:
[The Long Corridor]
Where: the castle's main corridor, walked alone after the night burn.
Story: it runs longer than by day, the same doors passing twice; no figure, only a walk that took eleven minutes when the bell says otherwise.
Told near the Bell Tower or after late Library sessions.

207.comment: Ghost Story - The Three O'Clock Knock
207.content:
[The Three O'Clock Knock]
Where: a dorm door, at three in the morning, in a dormitory that admits only its own students.
Rule: three evenly spaced knocks; count them and go back to sleep. It is never four, and nobody wants to learn what four means.
Students argue whether sound can even cross the door wards.

208.comment: Ghost Story - The Crying on the Water
208.content:
[The Crying on the Water]
Where: the Lake, after dark. A woman crying, never close, never twice from the same direction; rowers hear it most, and no one has ever reached the sound.
Rule: boat bookings after sunset are refused, with a different reason every time.
The Fishing Club blames distance.

209.content:
[The Night Student]
Where: the Lecture Hall tier, after curfew. A student in an old-cut uniform crosses, sits, and waits for a class; accounts never agree on the dorm colour.
Mostly placed in the breach year, so third-years refuse to tell it. It resurfaces every Remembrance Day.

210.content:
[Sunfizz] The soda every student drinks, sold at the Commissary and the Mall store in heavy glass bottles.
Price: 8 points, 2 back per returned bottle.
Taste: absurdly sweet.
Known for: confiscated in lectures; caps litter the Lecture Halls.

211.content:
[The Lucky Roll] The Canteen's free filled roll, baked in batches, no two fillings alike, nothing written down.
Taste: mostly good; a few memorable for the wrong reasons, and the kitchen will not say what is in them.
Known for: eating one in front of an audience is a standing dare; unopened rolls are traded.

212.content:
[Ardenne] The luxury marque in magical equipment: focuses, instruments, cases, measuring tools. Run by the Ardenne family.
Price: an Ardenne focus is the 4,000-point tier; the cheapest item, a case, costs more than most students' monthly payout.
Known for: marks its owner instantly as wealthy; never advertises.

213.content:
[Firetooth] A tin of hard sweets hot enough to make the eyes water, sold everywhere.
Price: 12 points.
Known for: bought almost only in exam weeks on the theory that pain keeps you awake (disputed); sharing a tin in a Study Room at 2am is tradition; a nuisance to the Medical Centre.

214.content:
[Nightwell] A small Mall coffee house with one famous order, the Vigil.
Price: 60 points.
Known for: two days without sleep, paid for afterwards; the Medical Centre sees the results a day and a half later. Exam-week staple.

215.content:
[The Oracle Shell] A palm-sized novelty shell sold at Merryhew's, the Mall's joke shop, that answers any spoken question with yes, no, or ask again later.
Price: 40 points.
Known for: transparently random, asked anyway, for jokes or 2am secrets. Real diviners find it insulting, which helps sales.

216.content:
[Merryhew's] The Mall's joke shop: itching charms, voice-changing sweets, illusion vermin, screaming boxes, fake exam results convincing enough to be banned twice.
Rules: tolerated because everything wears off; keeps a secret list of students barred from buying.

217.content:
[The Snug] A Mall eating house where every table is a partitioned private booth.
Known for: ordinary food, real privacy. Point loans, betting settlements, club trades, apologies and quiet negotiations; staff hear nothing. Booths by the hour, always a wait.

218.content:
[Dragonchess]
Play: starts as ordinary chess (drawn from chess and shogi) on floating checkered spheres over golden clockwork pedestals that materialise the pieces. The board reads the players and escalates: it unfolds into layers and the pieces fight autonomously in real time, so players outmanoeuvre both the opponent and the game.
Known for: rare sets; serious matches last days.

219.content: [Mana Grid] The academy runs on a grid drawn from the flow the seal already collects. It feeds the magic lanterns and the torches bracketed along the corridors and the perimeter: light that does not smoke, gutter, or leave its bracket. Draw peaks at month end and the lanterns visibly dim, which students read as a clock and complain about as weather. Nothing on the grid records or transmits anything; the Announcement Pillars are a separate sound working that only carries live voice. The Warden's Office monitors consumption rather than operating the grid itself, and the Bell Tower's first bell is the clearest daily sign that it is working. Most lanterns and wall torches are Caelmari-made, bought by the thousand.

221.content:
[Paid Work] Posts a student can take during term, all logged and all capped in hours so nobody earns near the top band.
- Canteen kitchen and serving: the most shifts and the least competition.
- Mail Tower sorting floor: heaviest on Sundays when the letters go out.
- Commissary counter: term start and exam weeks only.
- Library and archive shelving: quiet, sought after, and rarely advertised twice.
- Menagerie mucking out: pays the most because nobody wants it.
- Workshop repair: needs an actual skill and is paid accordingly.
- Potion Halls cleaning: supervised, strict disposal rules, good pay.
- Tutoring: arranged privately, paid in points or in favours.
Most posts pay twenty to forty points a shift. Openings go up on the Notice Board and are gone within a day. Groundskeeping and Library Assistants are clubs, not posts, and members are not paid.

222.content:
[Star Cookie] A star-shaped bakery biscuit.
Price: 8 points.
Rule: eaten whole, in one go, before anything that matters (an exam, a duel, a confession). Halves do not count.
Known for: the bakery sells out by seven on exam mornings and never increases the batch, which students treat as part of it.

223.content:
[The Founder's Hand]
Rule: touch the Founder's Statue's outstretched hand before an exam, always the hand, always on the way out.
Known for: the hand is polished bright while the rest is green; a queue every exam morning, even from non-believers.

224.content:
[Sleeping in the Library]
Story: fall asleep over a book and you wake somewhere else: a reading room with the wrong number of doors, shelves out of order, nobody else in the building.
Rule: sit still and sleep again; do not walk. Everyone who tells it woke the second time in their own chair.
Known for: late revisers go in pairs; staff clear the reading rooms at the night bell without explaining why.

225.content:
[Eating in the Forest]
Rule: share first. Leave a bite on the ground or a crust on a stump before the first mouthful.
Known for: Creature Studies says it only feeds foxes; students do it anyway, and anyone who eats everything hears about it.

226.content:
[Taken]
Story: what came through the Crack takes people by their names.
Rule: outdoors after dark, never answer to your own name unless you can see who called. Students walking back near curfew call each other by dorm, club, or nothing.
Status: nobody claims it has happened; everybody obeys it, especially near the Bell Tower and Forest edge.

229.content:
[Magical Beasts - Name List]
Grades: IV nuisance, III dangerous to a person, II dangerous to a group, I settlement-scale. Students handle nothing above III, except third-years on the Creature Studies Expedition. Vary the creature to the place; do not default to boars.
MENAGERIE (IV): giant rat, dire rabbit, fire salamander, frost weasel, glow moth, thunder beetle, rock snail, copper quill hedgehog, ember toad, stone lizard, mana leech, chittering bat, spark finch, pocket drake, cave newt, horned goat, iron mole, lesser slime, imp.
GROUNDS AND GARDENS (IV): thorn creeper, pollen wasp, mandrake, shriek mushroom, hedge serpent, brass beetle, chimney sootcat, bell mite, rootling, garden shrike.
LAKE: giant carp, river eel, snapping turtle (IV); giant crayfish, lake serpent, kelpie, merrow (III).
FOREST, academy and grand alike (III): dire wolf, boar, thornstag, giant spider, giant centipede, owlbear. Grand forest only: goblin hound (IV), harpy, forest troll, ashen lynx, mist wolf, lesser drake, cockatrice, gargoyle, torrent eel, echo bat, hush owl, spore shambler (III); chime toad (IV).
GRAND FOREST (II, expedition and hunting country): basilisk, manticore, wyvern, chimera, griffin, ogre, cave troll, dire bear, young hydra, giant scorpion, ironback boar, cinder wyrm, dread weaver, bone drake, roc, displacer cat, gorgon, rime elk, bloom maw.
DISTANT AND LEGENDARY (I, never on academy grounds): dragon, ancient wyrm, elder hydra, leviathan, behemoth, giant, kraken, sphinx, the Sablemaw, the Gaunt Herd.
GRAND FOREST (I): the Wendigo, which lives in the Gloaming of the Grand Vast Forest (its own entry); the one Grade I a student may ever meet, and nothing a student can beat.
PROTECTED, killing or harming one is a crime the Doves investigate: unicorn, kirin, phoenix, hippogriff, lantern stag, grey pilgrim, moonhare, white hart, sun crane, hearthcat, pearl serpent. Deep forest and remote country; Halvard's Menagerie holds none. Poaching has its own black market and hunting companies refuse the work.

230.content:
[Creature Studies Expedition]
When: Month 2 Week 3, Wednesday to Friday. The Creature Studies practical exam, led by Vallie Goredust; one airship per year level, each with two other members of staff aboard by rota, and the Doves travel along.
Where: the Grand Vast Forest (its own entries: a rainforest, mapped for the Expedition), half a day by airship; one ship per year level.
Teams: groups of four, graded together.
Wed: flight, then Base Camp (tents, cookfires, watch rotations) and gear prep.
Thu: from 08:00 each group is told its target (Years 1-2 Grade III, Year 3 Grade II) but not where to find it, heads out, and pitches its own camp in the wild wherever the hunt takes it; 24 hours. Staff shadow at a distance and pull out groups in trouble.
Fri: groups return to Base Camp by noon; break camp, fly home. Catches count dead or alive. A group that comes back without its target fails the practical and hears about it all year.
The evening before: the queue to touch the Founder's Statue's hand fills Founder's Park.
Bracelets: before the flight, staff bind every bracelet to a reading board in Vallie's command tent, which shows where each student is and their heartbeat. Staff watch it day and night and go to any group whose readings spike or stop. The binding is lifted on return. Inside the Grand Cave Network the reading fades past the first chamber.
Flare: every group also carries one red recall flare. Firing it is no failure: staff come within minutes and the group is marked on what it did before. A group that should have fired and did not is marked down harder.
Catches: live ones are marked, then released at the treeline (Halvard's Menagerie keeps Grade IV only); dead ones are sold to the Huntsmen's Lodge for the academy. Students carry coin; points do not work here.
Nights: Wednesday night everyone stays in Base Camp except the watch. Thursday the hunt runs through the night.
Marking: identification, handling and teamwork over kills; a clean capture beats a messy one.

231.content:
[Airships]
Use: the kingdom's long-distance transport, hired by the academy for anything past a day's ride: the Expedition, the Academy Trip, the long breaks, travel to the Kingdom and World Competitions.
Onboard: big enough to live on; glassed promenade, common room, canteen, washrooms and bathing stalls, one cabin per group of four; cargo, gear and beast pens below.
Crew: hired, not academy staff. Teachers take the forward cabins and count passengers at boarding and landing. Nothing aboard records or sends anything. Most airship lines on the continent are Yozakuran companies, and so are their crews.

232.content:
[Midterm]
When: Month 3 Week 1 and Month 9 Week 1, Monday to Thursday. Normal classes stop for the week.
Mon: Magic Theory, then Etiquette. Written.
Tue: History written; Potion Crafting practical (one brew from a sealed brief, marked on result and process).
Wed: Dark Magic Defense practical, each student against the teacher. Nobody is expected to win; the mark is for how long you hold.
Thu: Combat practical, students paired within their year, marked by combat role.
Creature Studies sits no midterm; it is marked on fieldwork.
Marks post at week's end; dorm ranking waits for end-of-semester results. In Month 9, Magic Theory may be replaced by a Magical & Science Fair score.

233.content:
[Club Festival]
When: Month 3 Week 2, Friday afternoon and all of Saturday.
What: every club runs a stand in the Main Courtyard: demonstrations, displays, contests, food. Duelling and sport clubs run exhibition matches, Alchemy and Smithing sell their work, Beast Handling brings out tame specimens, quieter clubs use displays and free samples. Club-funded, staffed in shifts.
Voting: every student and staff member gets one gold coin to drop at the best stand; nobody votes for their own club, advisors included. Winner announced at Saturday's close.
Prize: prestige only, plus better leverage for room space and budget all year.

234.content:
[Training Week]
When: Month 3 Week 3, Monday to Saturday, the week before the Dorm Competition.
Classes run normally. Curfew moves to 9pm and the Combat Grounds, duelling rings and practice halls stay open and supervised into the evening.
Taking part is optional. Students spar, drill and test builds against each other, freely across years and dorms.

235.content:
[Secret Fools Day]
When: Month 4 Week 1, Wednesday.
Dorm draw: each dorm has a box of its members' names. Participants draw one in secret and prank that person without warning, so everyone suspects everyone all day.
Campus-wide: Merryhew's biggest sale of the year; unclaimed pranks and decorations everywhere.
Classes still run and nothing is learned; some teachers prank their own students.
Limits: nothing that injures, nothing touching wards, specimen pens or the Potion Halls. The Doves ignore it unless something causes real damage.

236.content:
[End of Semester Exams]
When: Month 5 Week 1 and Month 11 Week 1, Monday to Thursday. No classes; one exam and nothing else.
Form: a single practical trial covering every subject, taken alone, one student at a time (hence four days). The course is rebuilt between runs.
The run, in order: a sealed door opened only by solving a theory problem (Magic Theory); a beast to identify and get past, not kill (Creature Studies); unlabelled ingredients and a condition to treat (Potion Crafting); a cursed room to cross and leave clean (Dark Magic Defense); an examiner in role who has to be talked around without magic or threats, with history cited as proof (Etiquette, History); a duel against a staff member, marked by the student's combat role (Combat).
Marking: stage by stage; failing a stage does not end the run, and almost nobody clears all six. Royal Inspectorate examiners watch from the gallery.

237.content:
[Results & Dorm Ranking]
When: Month 5 Week 2 Friday and Month 11 Week 1 Saturday.
Arbiter Hall assembly: the Headmaster and Vice Headmaster open it with speeches, then the trial results are given stage by stage, then the dorm ranking is recalculated from every member's marks and read aloud last. It holds until the next ranking day.
Evening: the Headmaster and Vice Headmaster speak, then the feast in the Ring Dining Hall.
Mood: one dorm celebrates, three eat anyway.

238.content:
[Mid-Year Break]
When: Month 5 Week 4, Monday to Sunday. No classes, no clubs.
Airships leave the first morning and return the last. Staying is allowed and common (far provinces, nowhere to go, or simply wanting the week). The canteen runs short hours and half the mall closes. A skeleton staff and the Warden stay to keep the seal fed.
Mood: quiet enough to hear the bells from anywhere.

239.content:
[Sports Day]
When: Month 6 Week 3, Saturday. No classes, no club block.
Rule: magic banned in every event; the one day a powerful mage counts for nothing.
Events: optional, open to anyone; most of the academy watches. Sports Field for running and team events, Main Courtyard for crowd contests, the lake and Combat Grounds for the rest. Sport clubs supply most favourites.
Medals: gold, silver, copper per event, tallied by dorm at day's end. Bragging rights for a year; no effect on dorm ranking.

240.content:
[Magical & Science Fair]
When: Month 7 Week 2, Friday and Saturday. Run by the first-year Magic Theory teacher.
What: stands in the Main Courtyard, solo or any group size: inventions, research, demonstrations, anything where magic meets science. Built through the week; Friday set-up and viewing, Saturday judging.
Judging: a staff panel questions and scores each stand. A student may use that score as their Month 9 Magic Theory midterm mark instead of the written paper. Group stands share one score.
Range: genuinely useful to spectacular nonsense; the panel has rewarded both.

241.content:
[Traveling Circus]
When: Month 8 Week 2, Thursday evening to Sunday. A hired touring company, not an academy event.
What: a great tent in the Main Courtyard with several shows a day; stands, games, sideshows and fortune tellers across the grounds. Stalls take points. Its great tent is striped crimson and cream, and its painted wagons park inside the wall by the Gatehouse.
Rules: classes run Friday and Saturday morning; curfew moves to 10pm.
Doves: dislike and monitor the large group of outsiders. Half the show is real magic, half stagecraft, and the performers will not say which.
Mood: the whole campus turned carnival.

242.content:
[Academy Showcase]
When: Month 8 Week 3, Thursday to Saturday.
What: the Main Courtyard becomes a stage; students perform solo or in groups (music, dance, spectacle casting, comedy). Optional; acts run all three days.
Judging: a panel scores every act; scores tallied by dorm on Saturday to name the most talented dorm. Bragging rights only.
Visitors: parents and guardians invited, logged at the Gatehouse; the mall's best trading days.
Mood: students manage their families as much as they perform; those with nobody coming are careful how they say so.

243.content:
[Academy Bazaar]
When: Month 9 Week 2, Thursday to Saturday.
What: invited traders from the capital, the provinces and abroad fill the Main Courtyard; the academy takes a cut. Stock the mall never carries: foreign sweets and drink, charms, imported components, odd instruments, foreign fashion, items nobody can explain.
- From abroad: Yozakuran tea, blossom sweets and a smith's katana far more students admire than can afford; Norvaine starglass lenses and scrying crystals; Caelmari mana lanterns, rune heaters and locks by the crate; Velmoran orchard preserves and court fashion; and Arslan brokers who change the coin of every crown. Each nation's traders keep to their colours: Yozakuran blossom pink and paper lanterns, Velmoran green and ivory, Arslan desert gold.
Prices: whatever the trader says; haggling expected; stalls take points. A year's savings can vanish in an afternoon.
Security: traders logged at the Gatehouse; the Doves watch the stock and the crowd.

244.content:
[Remembrance Day]
When: Month 10 Week 1, Tuesday. A Halvard day, not a kingdom one, marking the breach night two years ago.
Rules: nothing loud (no clubs, duelling, music, games, sport); classes run quietly; the Bell Tower keeps a slow pattern. Bouquets line the halls until evening.
Honoured: the students killed that night and the Warden who died resealing the Crack. Acting Warden Rei Kestrane attends.
Evening: on the Grassy Field and Hills, Headmaster Baelin, Vice Headmaster Althair and Acting Warden Rei speak, then the lantern release, one lantern per person.
Mood: memory for third-years, inherited for everyone else; silent until the last lantern is gone.

245.content:
[Harvest Festival]
When: Month 10 Week 4, Friday evening to Sunday. The largest festival of the year, the last loud thing before exams: the last harvest is in and winter is setting in, so the stalls run on braziers.
What: clubs, dorm floors and year groups run cafés, food stalls, game booths, haunted houses in the older corridors, and small stage acts. Nothing judged, no tally. The older corridors turned haunted houses glow a sickly green from outside.
Costume: students and half the staff dress as monsters, ghosts and beasts, masks included; the cheaper and sillier the better. Carved lanterns line every path.
Visitors: families invited all three days, logged at the Gatehouse.
Rules: curfew 11pm Friday and Saturday.
Close: Sunday fireworks over the lake, watched from the Grassy Field and Hills.

246.content:
[Sunreach Bay]
What: a small island and coastal nation, the world's playground, a full day from Halvard by airship.
Day: paradise; white beaches, turquoise lagoons, wholesome family fun.
Night: neon casinos, pleasure houses, every vice sold openly.
Policy: gives you whatever you came for and asks no questions.
Half its hotels are Yozakuran.

247.content:
[Academy Trip]
When: Month 11 Week 2, Monday to Saturday. All three years; the third-years' last trip as students.
Where: Sunreach Bay, a full day by airship each way (the Monday and the Saturday are spent flying, morning to night), a southern resort that stays warm all year: a few days of summer in Halvard's winter. Halvard has The Hanabira, a Yozakuran beachfront hotel on Coral Strand, four to a room; the rest is free time.
Days: Monday night the landing at the Skydock and check-in; Tuesday 09:00 the teachers' briefing in the hotel garden; free time until Friday; Friday 19:00 the farewell dinner at The Hanabira, then packing; Saturday 08:00 check out and board.
Rules: the teachers in the same hotel set a curfew at 22:00; leave the hotel only in groups of four. The city by day is allowed; its night side (the casinos and the Velvet Lanes) is out of bounds, which some students ignore every year.
Also there: Myrdath, Ashvale and Veyra send their students to Sunreach the same weeks.
Money: points do not work abroad; this is what a year of saving is for, and Sunreach is expensive.
Mood: students return tired, sunburnt and poorer than planned.
SUNREACH BAY INDEX — the city of the Academy Trip. Each place has its own entry when it comes up.
One city around a turquoise bay. By day a seaside paradise; from 18:00 to 06:00 the same streets are lit by rune-light: glowing coloured glass signs, painted banners under rune lamps, lanterns. No electricity anywhere.
Skydock: Skydock (airship masts, customs, the cliff road up to the Lighthouse).
Fisherman's Wharf: Fish Market (the seafood heart, grills by day, lantern stalls by night), Sea Dock (fishing fleet and the tour boats to the open sea).
Coral Strand: The Hanabira (Halvard's Yozakuran hotel, rooftop hot spring), Coral Beach (white sand, volleyball, fire dancers at night).
Sunpier: Sunpier (amusement pier, the Gull Run coaster), Tidehouse Aquarium (glass tunnel, the old turtle, violet at night).
Sunreach Crossing: Sunreach Crossing (six-street crossroads, glowing banners, game halls), Velvet Lanes (tiny stacked bars, singing rooms, the night market).
Casino Row: The Golden Tide (the great casino and its fountain lake), Plaza Dourada (pastel colonial square, custard tarts).
Cliffside Terraces: The Terraces (the islanders' stacked hillside town on stilts), Skyrail (red cable cars from the Crossing to the summit), Old Fort (ruin on the summit, stars at night).
Turquoise Lagoon: The Lagoon (warm turquoise water, rafts, a bar on stilts), Reef Gardens (glass-bottom boats, pearl divers), Shell Cove (hidden pink-sand cove).
West Cliffs: The Lighthouse (Norvaine keeper, up the cliff road from the Skydock), Sunset Cliffs (sunset, cliff diving), Glowtide Grotto (sea cave, glowing cavern and pool).
Open Sea: Open Sea (whales, dolphins, deep-sea fishing).
Walks between the parts (minutes on foot, the same both ways; a place inside one part is five to ten minutes from the next):
Skydock: Fisherman's Wharf 10, Coral Strand 15, Sunpier 25, Sunreach Crossing 25, West Cliffs 30, Casino Row 40, Cliffside Terraces 40, Turquoise Lagoon 60, Open Sea 70.
Fisherman's Wharf: Coral Strand 15, Sunreach Crossing 15, Sunpier 25, Casino Row 30, Cliffside Terraces 30, West Cliffs 40, Turquoise Lagoon 50, Open Sea 60.
Coral Strand: Sunpier 10, Sunreach Crossing 10, Casino Row 25, Cliffside Terraces 25, Turquoise Lagoon 45, West Cliffs 45, Open Sea 75.
Sunpier: Casino Row 15, Sunreach Crossing 20, Cliffside Terraces 35, Turquoise Lagoon 35, West Cliffs 55, Open Sea 85.
Sunreach Crossing: Casino Row 15, Cliffside Terraces 15, Turquoise Lagoon 35, West Cliffs 50, Open Sea 75.
Casino Row: Turquoise Lagoon 20, Cliffside Terraces 30, West Cliffs 65, Open Sea 90.
Cliffside Terraces: Turquoise Lagoon 35, West Cliffs 35, Open Sea 90.
Turquoise Lagoon: West Cliffs 70, Open Sea 110.
West Cliffs: Open Sea 100.
Getting around: horse carriages anywhere on land (6 coin) and water taxis between the shore parts (8 coin), both half the time; the Open Sea only by tour boat from the Sea Dock (15 coin each way). Points do not work; coin only.
Also in Sunreach these weeks: students of Myrdath, Ashvale and Veyra on their own trips, in the hotels along Coral Strand.
Rules for the narrator: who is met, street sights, hustlers, the sea and the dice are the engine's, listed in <now>; never add encounters or luck of your own, and never decide a bet.

248.content:
[Graduation]
When: Month 11 Week 4, Sunday, six days after the World Competition ends. Third-years leave; everyone attends.
Morning: Arbiter Hall ceremony. The Headmaster and Vice Headmaster speak, dorm heads read out their graduates, and each touches the Arbiter Stone a second and last time, the only time anyone touches it twice. Families, nobles and the Noble Houses' Liaison sit in the gallery.
Afternoon: recruitment tables from noble houses, the Royal Inspectorate, the Dovecote, the World Bank (Arslan Sultanate), hunting companies and city guilds, courting graduates they have tracked for three years. Offers made and refused on the spot.
Farewell market: from noon the Main Courtyard is a winter market for the day. Clubs and dorm floors run stalls of hot cider, roasted chestnuts, sweets and small farewell gifts under evergreen garlands and strings of lanterns, and families browse them between the ceremony and the tables. If there is snow, each dorm builds a snowman in its colours at the courtyard's edge. At the centre stands the Farewell Pine, a tall evergreen hung with ribbons: underclassmen tie one for each graduate they will miss, a wish written on it, and graduates look for their own before the feast. The market spills down into Founder's Park, the one winter day its lawns are full: more stalls between the paths, snowmen built by anyone with cold hands, and a small wooden stage by the statue where the Music Club plays through the afternoon and graduates are pulled up to sing.
Evening: the Headmaster and Vice Headmaster speak once more, then the feast; graduates leave by airship the next morning, the first day of the Kingdom-wide holiday. Their airship arrives at dusk and rides at anchor above the Grassy Field overnight, lit like a lantern.

249.content:
[Spirit Pact]
A negotiated contract: both sides must agree, a spirit cannot be forced, and the terms can be anything the two settle on. Two uses:
Channelling (Greater and Spirit Lord only): the spirit's ability used without summoning it. Costs mana per use and comes through far weaker than the spirit's own.
Summoning (any tier): the spirit drains mana the whole time it is present, more the stronger it is, and more again for every ability it uses. Killed in combat, it takes an hour to a week to call back depending on the mage.

253.content:
[Combat Roles]
Five roles used in Practical Magic (one class per role), exams and team competitions. A student may fill more than one, and then attends the class of the role they want most.
- Attack: deals the damage and finishes fights.
- Defense: shields, blocks and holds the line for the team.
- Healing: keeps allies standing mid-fight.
- Support: strengthens allies and weakens enemies.
- Control: restrains, disrupts and shapes the battlefield.

254.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Forest Clearing
254.content:
[Forest Clearing] A single oak called the Elder Oak stands in an open clearing in the middle of the Forest, so broad a dozen students holding hands cannot circle it, and older than the castle by anyone's guess. The canopy opens above the clearing, so the oak stands in full sun while the woods around it stay dim; the muffled quiet of the Forest gives way to birdsong at its edge, and gold motes drift in the light even on grey days. Its roots pull the ground's mana into slow currents unlike anywhere else on campus, and a wild field of rare flowers has spread across the clearing around it, in colours found nowhere else. The Gardening Club has tried transplanting them; they wilt within a day of leaving the clearing. A deer path leads in from the treeline, about thirty minutes' walk. Students come to read, nap between the roots, or be alone without feeling lost. The crust for Eating in the Forest goes on its roots. Patrols turn students back at dusk, and nobody answers their name out here after dark. In winter the clearing stays green and in flower while snow lies everywhere around it. Sitting among the oak's roots, a mage feels their mana refill like water finding its level.
Feel: sunlit, still, majestic, flower-scent and birdsong.
In spring: The flower field comes in weeks before anything else on campus.

255.content:
[Rooftop] The flat lead roofs of the castle core, joined by parapet walks and short stairs between the gables. Officially out of bounds. The only way up is a small locked door off the Bell Tower stair, and the trick of opening it is passed from older students to younger ones, never written down; being shown the way up means someone has decided you belong. From the parapet the whole academy lies open: the courtyards, the four dormitories, the Hills, the Lake, the Forest's dark edge, the white roofs of the Dovecote. At night the mana lanterns spread below like a lit map, and at month end you can watch them dim together. The campus's quiet romantic secret: couples come up for sunset and the lantern view, and a hidden corner behind the eastern gable is where confessions happen. Nobody who has been brought up here tells, and the rule is to leave a corner free if someone is already in it. Birds lift off just before each bell, and the lead hums underfoot when it rings. Staff walk the courtyards after curfew, never the roof.
Home of the Other Climber story.
Feel: wide sky, wind, sun-warm lead, a shared secret.
In summer: Every corner is taken at sunset.
In winter: The lead roofs ice over and even the couples stay away.

256.content:
[Headmaster's Office] At the end of the Faculty Offices corridor, a round room up a short stair, its tall windows over the Main Courtyard. Forty years of one Elf's tenure fill it: shelves layered deep with books, and letters and small gifts from graduates. In the window stands a sapling grown from the Elder Oak, forty years old and still knee-high. Students come only when it matters: serious discipline, a request to repeat a year, news no one wants to hear. The bench outside is where the real waiting happens. Visitors from the Royal Inspectorate and the Dovecote are received here, since the Headmaster has no authority inside the Dovecote's walls or past the Inspectorate's door. The door stands open whenever the Headmaster is in.
Feel: old wood, ink, green leaves, patient quiet.

257.content:
[Romantic Spots]
Spots: the Rooftop at sunset or under the lantern view, for those who have been shown the way up; the flower field around the Elder Oak in the Forest Clearing by day; the willow island on the Lake, rowed out to at dusk before the boathouse stops taking bookings, then watched glowing with fireflies from the shore; a booth at the Snug; the quieter back paths of Founder's Park.
Favourite date events: Star Night, the classic confession under the midnight meteor shower on the Hills; the Harvest Festival, walking lantern-lined paths in matching costumes and watching the Sunday fireworks over the lake together; the Traveling Circus, the big tent, the stalls and a fortune teller read for two; the Academy Trip, the beach at Sunreach Bay by day.

258.content:
[Staff Quarters] A separate stone house for the resident teaching staff (Dorm Heads live in their own dormitories instead), standing on its own beside the castle and joined to the castle's ground floor by a short covered walk: private rooms upstairs, and downstairs a shared parlour with mismatched armchairs, a kettle that is never cold, and a porch facing the Gardens. Where the Staff Room keeps students out, the Staff Quarters let them in: students may knock until the eight o'clock bell, and nothing said in the parlour counts as a consultation or a referral. It is where students come for help they would not ask for in class, advice about home, a second opinion on a club, or just tea with a teacher they like. Teachers here are off duty and act like it. Every door says something about who lives behind it: forest air draughting under Gavlan's, two teacups and a stack of theory on Layla's, and notes slid under Mimosa's, answered by morning. Vallie Goredust lives out by the Menagerie but holds court in the parlour anyway.
Feel: lamplight, tea, worn armchairs, lived-in.

259.content:
[Fire Dormitory] Home of the Elementalists (red vest). Red-tiled roof and a red banner over the door. A great hearth burns in its common room day and night, and the broad chimney stack rising above the front of the building is always warm, even in winter. Inside: a common area and personal rooms. Creed: "Through the Elements, Victory Is Ours."
Feel: hearth warmth, woodsmoke, stone.
In summer: The hearth burns anyway, and the common room is the hottest place on campus.
In winter: The hearth is the envy of the other three dormitories.

260.content:
[Light Dormitory] Home of the Mystics (yellow vest). Golden-tiled roof and a yellow banner over the door. Its inner court is roofed by a glass dome over the common area, which glows from within after dark. Inside: the glass dome common area plus personal rooms. Creed: "The Third Eye Lights The Way."
Feel: sunlight through glass, pale stone.
In summer: The dome turns the common area into a greenhouse by afternoon.
In winter: Snow slides off the warm glass dome, which glows brighter against the early dark.

261.content:
[Sky Dormitory] Home of the Occultists (blue vest). Deep-blue-tiled roof and a blue banner over the door. A single slender tower rises from one corner, and the building's enchanted walls let residents see the academy grounds from their rooms; from outside the windows shimmer faintly, like water. Inside: common area and personal rooms. Creed: "Together We Are Strong."
Stigma: Occult carries a reputation no other type does. Outsiders associate it with blood magic, demon summoning, and spirits bound against their will, and cannot always tell legal Occult practice from forbidden work. The Doves watch Occultists more closely than any other dorm, and Sky students are often the first suspected when something goes wrong. The creed reflects this: Sky students close ranks because few others will stand with them.
Feel: cool stone, shimmering windows.

262.content:
[Viridian Dormitory] Home of the Spiritualists (green vest). Green-tiled roof and a green banner over the door. An old oak fills its inner court, its crown rising above the roofline, with meditation stones set among its roots. Inside: common area, meditation rooms, personal rooms. Creed: "Know Thyself, Know Victory."
Feel: oak shade, rustling leaves, stone.
In spring: The inner oak comes into new leaf.
In summer: Deep shade over the meditation stones.
In autumn: The oak turns gold and leaves drift into the common area.
In winter: Bare branches over the roofline; the meditation stones sit under snow.

263.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Old Hut
263.content:
[Old Hut] A one-room timber hut on the far slope of the Hills, where the grass runs out against the Forest treeline. Nobody remembers who built it or when; the Groundskeeper's Lodge lists it as disused and not worth repairing, and leaves it standing. The roof sags, the door hangs from one hinge, and the cold hearth still holds old ash. It is where students go to share secrets: far from every building and path, with nobody walking past, and by long student custom what is said inside the Old Hut stays there. Generations of confessions have left initials carved into the inside walls. It also serves as shelter from sudden rain, and on Star Night it is claimed before sunset. After dark nobody lingers, since it sits right on the Forest edge where patrols walk and names are not answered.
Feel: weathered wood, wind through gaps, grass and pine.
In winter: Hardly anyone climbs to the Old Hut in winter: snow drifts against the door, the path over the Hills disappears, and a secret told there in the cold is one someone went to real trouble for.

264.comment: Academy Location - Student Life - Announcement Room
264.content:
[Announcement Room] A small booth-like room off the Club Rooms corridor on Floor 1, home of the Academy Newspaper club. A speaking rune set into the desk carries whatever is said into it, live, to the Announcement Pillars around the grounds; nothing is recorded. Students on duty open the day with a good-morning after the seven o'clock bell and give the noon, afternoon and evening greetings, the last just before the eight o'clock bell. In between they read out what staff, the Student Council and event organisers send down, plus whatever the student on duty decides is important, the most argued-about power any club holds. Outside class periods the Music Club plays live from the side room, and the whole campus hears it. Staff can take over the rune for anything urgent; during The Thinning lockdown it is how the academy speaks to everyone at once.
Feel: cramped, warm lamplight, sheet music and newsprint.

265.content: [Announcement Pillars] Slender stone pillars carved with sound runes, standing across the whole academy. They carry the live voice or music from the Announcement Room and nothing else: they cannot be spoken into, record nothing, and are a separate working from the mana grid. Their runes glow faintly while a broadcast is live. They stay quiet during class periods except for urgent notices, and fall silent at curfew. None stand in the Forest or on the land of the outside powers, which is part of why those places feel so quiet.

266.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Broken Statue
266.content:
[Broken Statue] A white marble statue standing in a stand of old trees between the Fire Dormitory and the Dovecote, off the path students take when they would rather not walk past the Dovecote's front. The figure has lost its head and one arm; the arm lies half-sunk in the moss at its feet, and moss and lichen have crept over the rest until the white shows only in patches. The inscription on its plinth has worn smooth. Who it depicted is unknown, and nobody on staff claims to know; students have theories and none of them agree. Groundskeeping leaves it exactly as it is. Light comes through the leaves in pieces, and the place is quieter than it should be for somewhere so close to the courtyard.
Feel: green shade, cold marble, moss, stillness.
<narrator_only>A hidden room lies beneath the statue. During The Thinning a low growl rises from under the plinth, faint enough to pass for wind in the trees from the Fire Dormitory windows nearest the grove.</narrator_only>

267.comment: Academy Location - Academic - The Sparring Pavilion
267.content:
[The Sparring Pavilion] A small round pavilion with a domed roof at the far corner of the Combat Grounds, the one building all four dorm training areas share. Inside: racks of training foci, ward-chalk and spare casting gear signed out by bracelet; benches, a water pump and a basic first-aid chest for the walk back after a hard session; a board of duel challenges and club standings. The club duels with spells inside warded rings, not staves. It is the Magic Duelling Club's headquarters, the standing exception to dorm separation, so it is the one place on the grounds where students of rival dorms share a bench. Gavlan Haverton, who advises the club, keeps a desk in the back. Unwritten rule: grudges from the rings are settled in the rings, never under the roof.
Feel: sweat, liniment, chalk dust, tired laughter.

268.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Fishing House
268.content:
[Fishing House] The Fishing Club's timber hut on the lake shore, three minutes' walk along the shore from the boathouse, full of rods, nets and tackle, with its own long dock built for fishing rather than boats. Behind it, a stone-edged pond raises fish for the Canteen kitchen and the Fishing Club's breeding projects. The club meets here; the dock is busiest at dawn, and quiet enough that people come to sit on it without a rod.
Feel: tar, wet rope, early mist on the water.
In winter: A stove burns in the hut, and the dawn regulars fish from the end of the dock through the mist.

269.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Willow Island
269.content:
[Willow Island] A small island in the middle of the lake with one great willow tree on it, reached only by a boat from the boathouse, which refuses bookings after dark. At night the willow glows in the distance from the many fireflies that live on the island, so anyone out there after dark was either rowed out before sunset or took a boat without asking.
Feel: still water, trailing leaves, firefly light.
In winter: The fireflies stay all winter, even over the ice, which Creature Studies cannot explain.

273.content:
[The Devoured Kingdom]
Story: thousands of years ago, a king made a pact with Azathoth, Lord of All, greatest of Asmoday's spirits. Its price was his whole kingdom, devoured to the last stone; the Primal Desert, where the Arslan Sultanate stands today, is what remains.
Told: everywhere, always beside the First Bargain.
Lesson: a lawful pact can still cost everything.
Status: the terms, the king and the kingdom's name are all forgotten.

274.comment: World Myth - The Four Who Saved the World
274.content:
[The Four Who Saved the World]
Story: when the First Bargain nearly ended the world, four heroes saved it: the King of Knights from the north, the Archmage from the east, the Lady of the Lake from the south, the Empress of the Fractured Vow from the west. They freed the lands the Demon King held, Eldrasil among them, and slew the Demon King. The first Gate, in the Demon Kingdom, they could not close; it stands open still, and the other Gates were sealed one by one in the years after.
Told: across the continent; each land calls its own hero the greatest. Eldrasil, in the east, claims the Archmage.
Lesson: no land saves the world alone.
Status: their names and faces are lost. Some say each carried one of the four fractured magics. The last Gate is no legend: Norvaine holds the line against what comes through it today.
<narrator_only>The Archmage's part was sealing what shone. Lucifer has called them the thief ever since.</narrator_only>

275.content:
[The First Bargain]
Story: when magic was still whole, a mortal bargained with something that shone brighter than any star and asked for all of magic. The bargain was kept to the letter. With all of magic in his hands he tore a Gate from his own land into the demon world, crowned himself the Demon King, and opened more Gates across the continent to loose his demons on every other nation, and the world nearly broke. Magic was then fractured into four; nearly every mage since is born to one type.
Told: everywhere; Dark Magic Defense opens its Pacting lesson with it.
Lesson: never make a pact with anything but a spirit.
Status: the mortal's name is forgotten; he is remembered only as the Demon King. The Cathedral says Asmoday fractured magic to save her world.
<narrator_only>What shone was Lucifer. Freed, he could give any magic to anyone again. He remembers the mortal fondly: the Demon King was his first bargain, and his favourite.</narrator_only>

276.content:
[The Holy Grail]
Story: a cup that grants any wish to whoever drinks from it. Some say the Lady of the Lake hid it after the First Bargain, so no one could wish the world broken again.
Told: everywhere; the favourite tale of treasure hunters.
Lesson: every wish has a shape the wisher did not see.
Status: where it is, what it looks like and whether it was ever real are unknown. It is not Ashvale's Elixir, which only heals.

277.comment: World Myth - The Shaping of the World
277.content:
[The Shaping of the World]
Story: before anything there was formless dark. Asmoday, Goddess of Creation, shaped it: first the spirits, then land, sea, sky and every living thing. Last, mortals were born from the soil of her world, and she gave them magic to shape things too.
Told: by the Cathedral word for word; the version most children grow up with.
Lesson: what you shape, you answer for.
Status: the Cathedral teaches it as truth; History Class leaves it to the Cathedral.
<narrator_only>The last line is the goddess wearing another's credit: Lucifer made magic, not Asmoday.</narrator_only>

278.content:
[Arslan Sultanate]
What: a sultanate in the Primal Desert, where the Devoured Kingdom once stood, and the money capital of the world. The desert grows nothing, so the whole country trades: bankers, brokers and moneylenders.
Known for: the World Bank, in its capital, which sets what every nation's coin is worth and lends to every crown, Eldrasil's included.
People: rich, exact, and very polite to anyone who owes them.
Status: the sand still turns up stones of the devoured kingdom. Nobody digs deeper than they have to.

279.content:
[Norvaine]
What: the richest kingdom of the north, with the strongest army on the continent. For generations its kings have held a pact with Yog-Sothoth, Lord of the Cosmos, a Spirit Lord; each heir inherits it with the crown.
War: Norvaine borders the Demon Kingdom and has held the demon front for as long as Norvaine has stood: a stalemate it cannot win and has never lost. It has the strongest army on the continent because it has never had a year of peace; most of its mages go to the front after their academy years.
Culture: Slavic in flavour: names like Vesna, Radomir, Mirko and Yarina, formal address by full name and father's name, long winters, birch and pine forests, onion-domed towers capped with starglass, black rye bread, beet soup and strong tea from a samovar, and a fierce hospitality to guests.
Export: starglass, a glass that holds the night sky; the finest telescope lenses and scrying crystals in the world.
Star Night: at midnight, over the royal castle, every star becomes an eye and every comet a tentacle.
Price: at that midnight Yog-Sothoth takes one person, the Chosen of the Cosmos, erased from the world's memory with every proof they existed and their soul. The kingdom remembers the rule, never the person.
People: they fear Yog-Sothoth, revere it, and bow to the sky every Star Night.
Status: nobody knows what the kings gained, or why the Chosen are taken.
<narrator_only>Norvaine's deepest secret is Koschei's Needle, an artifact found in the north that binds a soul: while it is intact, the one bound to it cannot be killed. After many failed bindings under Project Bessmertnik, one soul is bound to it now, Vesna's, and Norvaine uses her as a weapon that cannot be spent.</narrator_only>

333.content:
[Velmora]
What: an old kingdom on Eldrasil's northern border: green valleys and walled orchards between Eldrasil and the north. Its court is the most formal on the continent.
Known for: diplomats, dancing masters and etiquette tutors, hired by noble houses everywhere; anyone who wants to sound well-bred copies Velmoran court manners.
Ties: a long, quiet friendship with Eldrasil's crown.
Status: Velmorans abroad are gracious, careful, and never discuss their king.
<narrator_only>Behind the manners, the succession is a blood sport: the king lets his children fight for the crown, and betrayal, coups, assassination and blackmail are all fair. Whoever is left standing is heir.</narrator_only>

334.content:
[Caelmar]
What: a nation that is a single city in the west, as wide as a kingdom, built hundreds of floors into the sky and dozens deep into the earth, split into hundreds of districts and dozens of layers.
Rule: the king lives on the highest layer, above the clouds; the lower you live, the less you matter.
Below: the deepest layers are slums that never see the sun, where the city's refuse, workshops and outlaws collect.
Export: the continent's workshop. Mana lanterns, rune heaters, pens, locks, anything made by the thousand comes up from the lower layers.
Competitions: the academies' competitions are fought by the low-born and watched, sponsored and bet on by the high-born, who own teams the way they own racehorses; for a low-born fighter, winning is the one road up a layer.
Status: most Caelmari die on the layer they were born on.

335.content:
[Yozakura]
What: a kingdom in the south of the continent, mostly Beastkin, known for cherry blossoms and courtesy. Its companies run hotels, restaurants, bathhouses and airship lines all over the world.
Capital: Hanakaze, a city of wooden streets, red gates and sakura, with the Eternal Sakura at its heart, in bloom all year.
Rule: the throne is won, not inherited. A grand tournament crowns the ruler, titled Alpha, who reigns until beaten in the next one.
Known for: a passion for competing in everything, from academy duels to cooking contests; its team is always a favourite at the World Competition. Its smiths forge the katana, the finest blade a mage can hold.
Status: a Yozakuran never refuses a fair challenge.

336.content:
[Student Council Election]
When: Month 10 Week 3, Monday through Saturday. The election chooses next year's Student Council President and Vice President.
Campaign, Monday-Thursday: Classes run as usual. The serving Council nominees campaign outside class through dorm conversations, brochures, posters and public promises. The current President and Vice President oversee the election; campaigning does not transfer their authority.
