Year 1 nominees: Florian Villeneuve of Sky and Dante Kleinn of Light, both second-years and Council members since the start of the year. Florian promises visible results and stronger club support; Dante promises consistent rules and safer students.
<%_ } else if (_y === 2) { const second = _p.Second === (getvar('stat_data.Player.Profile.Name') || '{{user}}') ? '{{user}}' : 'Percival Applethorne'; const dorm = second === '{{user}}' ? (getvar('stat_data.Player.Profile.Dorm') || 'their dorm') : 'Viridian'; _%>
Year 2 nominees: Caralynn Veyturone of Fire and <%- second %> of <%- dorm %>, both second-years and Council members since the start of the year. Caralynn promises a Halvard the whole kingdom talks about: bigger festivals, a proper stage and the academy's name in every newspaper. <%- second === '{{user}}' ? '{{user}} writes their own platform.' : 'Percival promises a code of chivalry for every student: nobody left behind, the weak protected, and a knight’s oath at every Entrance Event.' %>
<%_ } else { _%>
Year 3 nominees: Hadrian Quelloris of Light and Nerys Silvarenne of Fire, both second-years and Council members since the start of the year. Hadrian promises efficiency: fewer meetings, shorter queues for the deserving, and rules that exist for a reason. Nerys promises, in the same flat voice, a weekly bread-sculpture competition and a Canteen Lucky Roll she has baked herself; at the debate she answers every question in flawless court speech.
<%_ } } _%>
Debate, Friday: Classes run as usual. After the last class, 16:00-18:00, the nominees debate in the Seminar Rooms and answer students' questions.
Voting, Saturday: Morning Etiquette runs as usual. Council members meet 10:00-12:00 in place of Study Hall, unless required to attend remedial. The 13:00-16:00 club block is replaced academy-wide by private presidential voting in the Main Courtyard; no ordinary club meeting takes place that afternoon.
Results, Saturday: After the ballots are counted, the result is announced in the Main Courtyard. The winner becomes President-elect and names the losing candidate Vice President-elect. {{user}} has one vote, not automatic control of the result.
Handover: The serving President and Vice President remain in office through Graduation; their successors take office at the start of the next school year.

337.content:
[The Thirteenth Stroke]
Where: anywhere outdoors after the eight o'clock bell.
Story: the Bell Tower sometimes strikes once more than the hour, a single stroke after the rest, when no one is in the tower.
Rule: count the strokes. If there is one too many, go indoors and do not count again that night.
Known for: nobody agrees on what the extra stroke is for; the bell ringers say the mechanism settles, and never ring it themselves.

338.content:
[The Night Swimmer]
Where: the Swimming Pool after dark, most often in winter when the rune-warmed water steams.
Story: someone swims steady lengths through the steam, the lane rope lifting as they pass, but when the steam clears the water is empty and still.
Rule: never swim alone after dark, and do not call out to them.
Known for: the Swimming Club claims the fastest lap on record and will not say who swam it.

339.content:
[The Walking Lantern]
Where: the Grassy Field and Hills, after dark.
Story: a single lantern light crosses the ridge at walking pace with no one carrying it, and stops when anyone stops to watch.
Rule: do not walk toward it, and do not follow it towards the Forest.
Known for: the Camping Club pitches on the lower slope after dusk and will not say why.

340.comment: Ghost Story - Breath on the Glass
340.content:
[Breath on the Glass]
Where: inside the Gardens' greenhouses, in the late afternoon and evening.
Story: the glass fogs from the inside, as if someone warm stood close to it, around a handprint that belongs to nobody present.
Rule: do not press your own hand over it, and do not sleep in the greenhouses.
Known for: the Gardening Club blames the heat pipes, and still leaves in pairs.

341.comment: Ghost Story - When the Pens Go Quiet
341.content:
[When the Pens Go Quiet]
Where: the Menagerie, from dusk into the night.
Story: every animal in the pens falls silent at once and turns to face the Forest, and stays that way for a long moment before the noise comes back.
Rule: when the pens go quiet, walk away in the other direction and do not look where they are looking.
Known for: the handlers call it weather sense; the Creature Studies teacher does not call it anything.

342.content:
[The Faraway Laugh]
Where: Founder's Park and the tree-lined paths, after dark.
Story: a woman laughs somewhere up in the old trees. The laugh always sounds far away.
Rule: the fainter it sounds, the closer she is. If it sounds far, walk the other way at once and do not look up.
Known for: students who hear it say it was only an owl, and take the long way round for a week.

343.content:
[The Polite Walker]
Where: the long paths out to the far grounds (the Gardens to the lake, the courtyard to the Hills), at dusk and after dark.
Story: footsteps fall in behind whoever walks alone, matching their pace, stopping when they stop. Turning round shows an empty path.
Rule: step off the path and say "after you". The steps go on past, and the path is yours again.
Known for: seniors teach first-years the words on their first walk to the lake, and laugh while they do it.

344.content:
[The Last Bed]
Where: the Medical Centre, at night, for students kept in overnight.
Story: the curtain round the last bed on the ward is drawn, and someone behind it breathes slowly in their sleep. The ward register says that bed is empty.
Rule: never open the last curtain. Ask the night nurse in the morning; she will tell you it was empty, and she will be kind about it.
Known for: patients who are well enough ask to be moved nearer the door.

345.content:
[The Other Climber]
Where: the Rooftop, at night.
Story: someone sits on the far gable in exactly your posture, wearing your dorm's vest, looking out over the grounds as you are.
Rule: leave the roof before they turn round, and do not come up again that night.
Known for: why students who know the way up never go up alone.

346.content:
[The Applause]
Where: the old amphitheatre off the Club Rooms corridor, during a late rehearsal.
Story: at the end of a scene, applause comes from the empty upper tiers, and one seat up there has been folded down.
Rule: bow, and end the rehearsal. Do not run the scene again that night.
Known for: the Theatre Troupe bows to the empty tiers at the end of every rehearsal, and calls it tradition.

347.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Spirit Path
347.content:
[Spirit Path] A narrow footpath that leaves the grounds behind the Gymnasium and winds through old trees along the eastern edge of the academy, a loop short enough to walk in a quarter of an hour. Spirits like it here: the air under the trees is still and green, lesser spirits drift among the roots and branches, and small stone cairns that students have stacked over the years mark the way. Spirit users bring their pact partners here to let them out for a short walk. It is also where beginners come to meet a lesser spirit and try their first Spirit Pact; the custom is to go slowly, offer something small, and let the spirit choose. Almost any Occult student can bond a lesser spirit; a pact is a lasting contract, and the Occult teachers expect to be told of one. Anyone may come to watch: a stone bench at each bend faces the trees, and at dusk and dawn the lesser spirits are easy to see, a flicker in the ferns, a small light keeping pace along a branch. Most are shy; now and then one comes close out of curiosity, and it is considered lucky to be looked over and left in peace.
Feel: green, dappled, hushed, quietly watched (never unkindly).
In spring: Lesser spirits are thickest when the new leaves come; the path is busy with first-years.
In autumn: Fallen leaves stir on windless days. It is only the spirits.
In winter: Snow shows small tracks that stop in the middle of the path.

360.content:
[GRAND VAST FOREST INDEX]
What: Eldrasil's great rainforest, half a day from Halvard by airship, so vast that crossing it takes weeks and nobody has walked all of it. Hunting-company country. Halvard comes once a year, for the Creature Studies Expedition (Month 2 Week 3), and uses only its southern rim: from Base Camp to the farthest point of that country is about half a day on foot.
Landmark: the Old Heart, a single giant tree at the rim's northern edge, rising far above the canopy and seen from anywhere in the southern forest; everyone steers by it. Beyond it the deep forest runs on, unmapped.
Climate: warm and wet all year. Mornings start in mist, the air is heavy and humid, and most afternoons a downpour comes through the canopy; nothing ever fully dries. Buttress-rooted giants, palms, tree ferns, hanging vines and moss on everything.
Places: Base Camp (the meadow at the southern edge: tents, the command tent, the Huntsmen's Lodge), The Wildwood (the ordinary rainforest west, north and east of Base Camp), Blightbriar (poisoned thorns and spore fungus), The Gloaming (the oldest, darkest stand, where noon looks like dusk), Silverstair Falls (the Silverrun river falling in a dozen tiers), Jade Terraces (hundreds of cold stepped pools above the falls), Grand Cave Network (a cliff mouth onto caves nobody has mapped), The Old Heart (the single giant tree at the northern edge). Each has its own entry when it comes up.
Neighbours (hours on foot): Base Camp – the Wildwood (west) 2, the Wildwood (north) 2, the Wildwood (east) 2. The Wildwood (north) – the Wildwood (west) 2.5, the Wildwood (east) 2.5, the Gloaming 3.5. The Wildwood (west) – Blightbriar 3. The Wildwood (east) – Silverstair Falls 4 (along the river). Blightbriar – the Gloaming 2.5, the Grand Cave Network 5. The Gloaming – Silverstair Falls 3.5, the Grand Cave Network 4, the Old Heart 5. Silverstair Falls – the Jade Terraces 1.5 (a climb). The Jade Terraces – the Old Heart 4. The Grand Cave Network – the Old Heart 5. Any other walk passes through the places between.
Shortest walks (hours, the same both ways):
Base Camp: the Wildwood (north) 2, the Wildwood (west) 2, the Wildwood (east) 2, Blightbriar 5, the Gloaming 5.5, Silverstair Falls 6, the Jade Terraces 7.5, the Grand Cave Network 9.5, the Old Heart 10.5.
The Wildwood (north): the Wildwood (west) 2.5, the Wildwood (east) 2.5, the Gloaming 3.5, Blightbriar 5.5, Silverstair Falls 6.5, the Grand Cave Network 7.5, the Jade Terraces 8, the Old Heart 8.5.
The Wildwood (west): Blightbriar 3, the Wildwood (east) 4, the Gloaming 5.5, Silverstair Falls 8, the Grand Cave Network 8, the Jade Terraces 9.5, the Old Heart 10.5.
The Wildwood (east): Silverstair Falls 4, the Jade Terraces 5.5, the Gloaming 6, Blightbriar 7, the Old Heart 9.5, the Grand Cave Network 10.
Blightbriar: the Gloaming 2.5, the Grand Cave Network 5, Silverstair Falls 6, the Jade Terraces 7.5, the Old Heart 7.5.
The Gloaming: Silverstair Falls 3.5, the Grand Cave Network 4, the Jade Terraces 5, the Old Heart 5.
Silverstair Falls: the Jade Terraces 1.5, the Old Heart 5.5, the Grand Cave Network 7.5.
The Jade Terraces: the Old Heart 4, the Grand Cave Network 9.
The Grand Cave Network: the Old Heart 5.
Walking costs stamina; half a day on foot without rest leaves anyone exhausted. The three Wildwood stretches (west, north, east) are one forest in three directions from Base Camp.
Rules for the narrator: the engine decides when the assigned target and any other beast appear (<now> says so). Never bring the target in on your own, never let a beast appear because it would be convenient, and never tell {{user}} where a beast lives: let tracks, class knowledge and the signs <now> gives show the way. Possible encounters in a place entry are what may appear there, not what is waiting. Every walk takes its hours on the clock; nobody crosses this forest in minutes.

361.content:
[Base Camp] A wide meadow at the forest's southern edge where the three academy airships ride at anchor; the Expedition's start and end. Tents in three rings, one per year level, around a central fire and Vallie's command tent with the bracelet reading board; a marking table where catches are logged and caged; watch posts at the corners. On its edge stands the Huntsmen's Lodge, a timber lodge the hunting companies share: smokehouse, weighing hook, and a counter selling rope, bait, salves, lamp oil and cloth spore masks for coin. Company hunters pass through and size up the students. Every way out of camp leads into the Wildwood: west, north or east.
Feel: woodsmoke, wet canvas, nervous laughter, the ships creaking overhead.
Possible encounters (rare, the camp is guarded): goblin hound (IV), dire wolf (III).

362.content:
[The Wildwood] The ordinary rainforest that fills everything between the named places: broadleaf giants on buttress roots, palms and tree ferns underneath, vines hanging to the ground, deer paths, deadfall, muddy hollows churned by boar, the odd clearing where a storm took the trees down. It is ordinary only by this forest's standards. Three stretches of it are named on the map, west, north and east of Base Camp; they are the same forest, only in different directions. Vallie tells every group about ironback boars before they leave camp.
Feel: birdsong that stops when something bigger moves.
Possible encounters: goblin hound (IV); dire wolf, boar, thornstag, owlbear, forest troll (III); ironback boar, dire bear, ogre, chimera (II).

363.content:
[Blightbriar] A stretch of the forest gone wrong: thorn thickets with poisoned barbs, fungus in shelves and bulbs and towers, and puffs of spore that hang in the air and burn the throat. Walking it without a face cloth leaves anyone coughing and drained. The danger here is mostly the plants.
Feel: sweet rot, itching skin, everything faintly moving.
Possible encounters: thorn creeper, shriek mushroom (IV); spore shambler (a dead animal walked by fungus threads) (III); bloom maw (a cart-sized carnivorous flower that lures with scent; it does not move, you come to it), manticore (II).

364.content:
[The Gloaming] The oldest, thickest stand of the rainforest: trunks wider than towers, moss and hanging vines over everything, a canopy so dense that noon looks like dusk and pale fungi give the only light. Few people come here, and it feels it: no trails, no cut wood, no sound of anyone. Hunting companies do not take work in the Gloaming.
Feel: green dark, damp, the sense that nobody has stood here in years.
Possible encounters: ashen lynx, hush owl (wings as wide as a cart, flies without a sound, drops from the dark canopy), giant spider (III); displacer cat, dread weaver (II). The Wendigo lives here.

365.content:
[Silverstair Falls] The Silverrun river drops over a wide cliff in a dozen broad tiers, each with its own plunge pool; spray hangs over the whole stair, rainbows by day and mist by morning. Climbing the stair to the Jade Terraces takes an hour and a half and wet hands.
Feel: roar of water, soaked to the skin, rainbows.
Possible encounters: mist wolf, kelpie, torrent eel (rides the falls and strikes with a jolt), harpy (III); griffin, roc, wyvern (nest on the cliff) (II).

366.content:
[Jade Terraces] Above the falls, a valley of stepped pools rimmed in pale gold stone, hundreds of them, each a different blue or green. The springs that feed the pools run cold, the one cool place in the forest. Animal-shaped stones stand in some of the pools; they are not carvings.
Feel: colour, stillness, steam on cold mornings.
Possible encounters: chime toad (rings like glass at dusk) (IV); cockatrice (III); young hydra, gorgon, rime elk (comes down to the cold pools at dawn) (II). A pearl serpent has been seen here, which is protected.

367.comment: Grand Vast Forest - Grand Cave Network
367.content:
[Grand Cave Network] A mouth in a cliff wall at the forest's north-west, wide enough to fly an airship into, opening onto caves said to run as far as the forest itself; nobody has mapped the end. Groups often pitch their tents just inside the mouth, dry and out of the wind. Staff chalk a line across the first chamber: no group goes past it. Warm air rises from somewhere below.
Feel: cold breath from below, dripping, an echo that answers late.
Possible encounters: giant centipede, echo bat (its shriek stuns), gargoyle and lesser drake (on the cliff face) (III); cave troll, basilisk, giant scorpion, bone drake, cinder wyrm (II).

368.comment: Grand Vast Forest - The Old Heart
368.content:
[The Old Heart] A single giant tree at the northern edge of the Expedition country, its trunk wider than the Main Courtyard, rising far above the canopy and seen from anywhere in the southern forest. Past it the deep forest begins, unmapped and weeks across. The protected beasts live around it; harming one is a crime the Doves investigate. No student goes, and no hunting company takes work there. Rumour says poachers do.
Feel: silver light, absolute quiet, the sense of being allowed in.
Possible encounters (never hunted): unicorn, lantern stag, moonhare, white hart, grey pilgrim. The Wendigo is sometimes seen at its edge.

369.content:
[The Wendigo] Grade I. A gaunt humanoid about three metres tall: grey-white skin drawn tight over bone, a deer's skull for a head, with antlers and a dim light in the sockets, and long clawed fingers. The air turns cold around it, frost forms where it stands, and it smells of rot. It speaks in the voices of people it has heard. It lives in the Gloaming of the Grand Vast Forest and is sometimes seen at the edge of the Old Heart.
Adapts: every spell of a kind (an element or a school) that has already hit it this fight does a fifth less than the one before: the first in full, then 80%, 60%, 40%, and 20% from the fifth on, never less. A new kind of spell starts again at full. It forgets after a day without a fight. Weapons do not make it adapt, but its hide is Grade I hard. Only overwhelming power (a Gareth Valkaryn) can force a way through a kind it has learned.
Behaviour: territorial. It stalks first and calls in borrowed voices, then tests intruders and drives them out; it does not follow anyone out of the Gloaming. Hunting companies do not take work there because of it.

370.content:
[AVALON INDEX — the capital. Each place has its own entry when it comes up.]
Avalon is the capital of Eldrasil and its largest city, some two hours from Halvard by airship. A round city of white stone on a gentle hill, inside one great white wall with four gates; the Great Gate in the south faces the Skyport. Past the wall there are no more walls: the city is laid out in rings by its streets alone, each ring a little higher than the one outside it, rising to Eldrasil Castle on its hill, which can be seen from every street.
Rings, from the castle out: the Noble Ring, the houses of the noble families on the castle's terraces; the Crown Ring, where the kingdom is run, around Crown Square; and the Lower City, the widest ring by far, where most of Avalon lives, works, shops and plays. Great avenues run from the gates to Crown Square, and the Ring Boulevard circles the Lower City just inside the wall; between them lie homes, workshops and the quarters visitors come for.
The White Line: a band of white marble set into every street where the Noble Ring begins. The Royal Guard stands on it. Nobody crosses without a royal summons or a noble's household badge, and the guards do not argue; the Doves are never far away. Students never cross it, except the team that wins the Kingdom Competition, received by the King at the castle.
The city was rebuilt in white after the War of Independence. Old Town alone keeps the grey stone of the years before, left as it was on purpose. Royal banners, deep blue and gold, fly from the castle towers; on Crowning Day they hang along every avenue.
The Herald Spires: seven tall white spires across the city, the city-sized version of the academy's announcement pillars. Each carries the same broadcast at once, live and never recorded: royal proclamations, the noon news, a bell and a few bars of music on every hour, and on Crowning Day the King's own voice. At night they glow faintly. The Great Spire in the north is the one the public may climb.
The city map (parts, then their places): Eldrasil Castle: Eldrasil Castle (the royal seat on the hill), Noble Ring (the noble houses on the castle terraces). Crown Square: Crown Square (the great square, the King's speech), Grand Cathedral (the kingdom's cathedral), The Chancery (the crown's offices and courts), High Dovecote (the Doves' tower), Royal Bank (the kingdom's bank). Great Gate: Skyport (airship masts outside the Great Gate), Gilded Arcade (glass-roofed shopping arcades). Lantern Quarter: Lantern Market (the biggest market, under lanterns), Spellwright Row (the magic trades). Old Town: Old Town (the grey old quarter), Skywheel Fair (the fairground and its giant wheel), The Great Spire (the tallest Herald Spire, open to climb). Garden of Avalon: Garden of Avalon (the great garden and the Archmage statue), Grand Theatre (the domed opera house). Arena Quarter: Royal Arena (the Kingdom Competition's stadium), Whitestone Hotel (where the four academies' teams stay). Kingsmeadow (beyond the Great Gate; open only for the Kingdom Competition's round one): Judges' Pavilion (the panel's white pavilion, start and sunset hand-in), Long Meadow (open grass to the horizon, nowhere to hide), Willow Brook (a willow-lined stream with stepping stones), Old Orchard (a crown orchard gone half wild), Bramble Hollow (a sunken thicket, slow going), Standing Stones (an old stone ring on a rise), Reed Marsh (reed beds and black water, wet to the knee), Beacon Hill (the high point, a cold beacon and a view). The Undercroft (under the Royal Arena; open only for the Kingdom Competition's round two): Undercroft Gates (three iron gates under the arena, one per team), Undercroft Room 1 (the Pillar Hall), Undercroft Room 2 (the Cistern), Undercroft Room 3 (the old Armoury), Undercroft Room 4 (the sunken Chapel), Undercroft Room 5 (the Gallery over a drop), Undercroft Room 6 (the Kennels), Undercroft Room 7 (the cold Furnace room), Undercroft Room 8 (the Vault), Undercroft Room 9 (the Pit), Undercroft Room 10 (the Deep Hall).
Walks between the parts (minutes on foot, the same both ways; a place inside one part is five to fifteen minutes from the next):
Eldrasil Castle: Crown Square 45, Great Gate 70, Lantern Quarter 80, Arena Quarter 85, The Undercroft 90, Kingsmeadow 100, Old Town 120, Garden of Avalon 120.
Crown Square: Great Gate 25, Lantern Quarter 35, Arena Quarter 40, The Undercroft 45, Kingsmeadow 55, Old Town 75, Garden of Avalon 75.
Great Gate: Kingsmeadow 30, Arena Quarter 35, Lantern Quarter 40, The Undercroft 40, Garden of Avalon 80, Old Town 90.
Lantern Quarter: Old Town 50, Kingsmeadow 70, Arena Quarter 75, The Undercroft 80, Garden of Avalon 100.
Old Town: Garden of Avalon 50, Arena Quarter 95, The Undercroft 100, Kingsmeadow 120.
Garden of Avalon: Arena Quarter 45, The Undercroft 50, Kingsmeadow 110.
Arena Quarter: The Undercroft 5, Kingsmeadow 65.
Kingsmeadow: The Undercroft 70.
Getting around: on foot, or by hire carriage from the stands at the Skyport, Crown Square and every quarter: half the time, for coin. Bracelet points do not work in Avalon; students carry coin, changed at the Banking House before they leave.
Rules for the narrator: what happens in the streets each hour (pickpockets, processions, students of the other academies, a raid) is the engine's, listed in <now>; never add trouble or luck of your own. Crowds, sellers, music, smells and colour are yours. Every walk takes its minutes on the clock. {{user}} never crosses the White Line unless <now> says the team was summoned.

371.content: [Eldrasil Castle] The royal seat at the top of the hill, white towers higher than anything in the city but the Great Spire, deep blue and gold banners on every tower. The King lives and rules here. The royal road climbs to it from Crown Square through the Noble Ring.

372.content: [Noble Ring] The townhouses of the noble families on the terraces around the castle: gardens behind white walls, quiet streets, private guards at the gates. The Noble Houses' Liaison keeps its offices here.

373.content:
[Crown Square] The great square at the foot of the castle hill, where Crown Avenue ends and every avenue of the city meets the Crown Ring. The parade finishes here on Crowning Day, the Royal Mages at its head, and the King speaks from the dais on the White Line; the Herald Spires carry the speech to the whole city. Fountains, a column to the War of Independence, food stalls on holidays.
Feel: The heart of the kingdom, in white stone and blue banners.

374.content: [Grand Cathedral] The house of Asmoday for the whole kingdom, white and immense, its nave open to anyone. Every cathedral in Eldrasil, Halvard's included, answers to it. Sermons on the hour on holy days; the registry of oaths sworn in the capital is kept in its undercroft.

375.content: [The Chancery] The crown's offices in one long white building around a courtyard: ministries, courts, the Royal Inspectorate's headquarters, the royal archive. Open to the public in its front halls for petitions; nobody goes in for fun.

376.content:
[Avalon — The Rookery]
The Rookery: Avalon's underbelly, a warren of old cellars, cisterns and smugglers' tunnels beneath Old Town, older than the white city above it. Its people call themselves rooks, a joke at the Doves' expense. A black market (stolen goods, contraband, unlicensed components, forged papers), gambling dens, a fighting pit where unlawful duels are fought for coin, and brokers who sell information to anyone. Lantern-lit, crowded, polite in its own way: rooks do not rob guests who behave, and they never forget a face that brings the Watch. Students are forbidden to go there. Buying or practising a forbidden art there is still arrest, as everywhere; being caught there is a serious offence for a student.
<narrator_only>The way in: the cellar door behind the bar of the Drowned Rat, a tavern on the lowest lane of Old Town; the barkeep opens it for anyone who asks for "the cellar wine". A few Old Town locals will point the way for coin; nobody else will. The City Watch raids the Rookery now and then (the engine decides when, in <now>), and the rooks usually hear it coming.</narrator_only>

377.content:
[Avalon — the Royal Mages on Crowning Day]
The Royal Mages, the Crown's own mages, lead the Crowning Day parade: ranks in white and deep blue, the silver star of the order on every collar, casting light and colour over Crown Avenue as they march. The youngest of them, Tsubaki Hoshikage, a wolf Beastkin with a katana, marches among them.
(Before campaign Year 2) Tsubaki Hoshikage this year: seventeen, long white hair tied back badly, grey wolf ears and tail, calm gold eyes, a katana in a plain black scabbard, the silver star on her collar. Frank, calm, brief; introduces herself as "Tsubaki Hoshikage. Royal Mage. Do you spar?" A genius with the sword who cannot find her way anywhere and does not understand hints or jokes. She is not a Halvard student yet: the Crown sends her there next year.

378.content: [Airship: Promenade Deck] The glassed gallery that wraps the airship's bow and runs down both sides: brass rails, padded benches under the windows, and nothing between the passengers and the sky but the glass. The bow end is the best view on the ship and the first place every student runs to at boarding; by the second hour it is the quietest. The glass is cold to the touch at height and the deck hums faintly underfoot. Yozakuran stewards walk it with tea on the long flights. The teachers stroll here too, which makes it the safest place on board to be seen talking to someone and the worst place to say anything private. Past the bow, a door marked in Yozakuran and Common leads to the bridge: crew only.

379.content: [Airship: Common Room] The ship's heart, midships: a long low room of lacquered wood with low tables and floor cushions in the Yozakuran style. At one end, a canteen counter where the stewards serve set meals included in the fare and tea that never runs out; beside it a small bar of polished dark wood, drinks and sweets for coin. The bar keeps the academy's rule: students drink only on the rest day and in the holidays, and the stewards check the bracelet first. In the far corner, a small raised stage with a lamp rail: usually a crew musician plays, but anyone can chalk their name on the board beside it and take a turn (a song, a trick, a little spellwork, a duel of rhymes), and the teachers borrow it for announcements. A shelf of worn board games and card decks. Every year level and dorm ends up here; it is where rivalries carry on in lowered voices and seating plans fall apart by the second hour. The crew counts passengers here at boarding. A hatch behind the counter leads down to the galley: crew only.

380.content: [Airship: Cabin Deck] A narrow corridor of numbered doors, one cabin to each group of four: two bunks stacked on each side, a round porthole, four lockers and a fold-down table. Thin walls; everyone hears the cabin next door laugh. At the far end are the washrooms and the bathing stalls, hot water piped from the engines, a Yozakuran touch every student remembers. On long flights it is where people sleep, sulk, study or hide. At the aft end a steep ladder goes down to the Cargo Hold. The forward end, past a curtain, holds the teachers' cabins: knock or don't go. Nothing aboard records or sends anything.

381.content: [Airship: Cargo Hold] The bottom of the ship, down a steep ladder from the aft end of the Cabin Deck: a long dim hold of crates in cargo nets, racks of luggage and gear strapped to the ribs of the hull. Cold, and the loudest place aboard: the engines' hum comes up through the floor. Passengers may come down for their luggage. A Yozakuran quartermaster keeps the hold and grumbles at everyone who does, but sends no one away. The teachers rarely come down, which makes it the most private place on the ship and the reason couples, plotters and the seasick end up here. What it carries changes with the route: tents, cookfires and camp gear on the way to the forest, the same gear and muddier on the way home; the academy's banners and spare uniforms on the way to Avalon; on the way back from Sunreach, more luggage than left Halvard, and the crates of what the teachers confiscated. A door at the bow end of the hold leads to the engine room: crew only.

382.content:
[The Demon Kingdom]
What: a land in the far north beyond Norvaine, where the last open Gate to the demon world stands. Demons hold it; whatever people lived there are long gone.
History, not myth: there were once many Gates, and their demons overran half the continent, Eldrasil among them. One by one the Gates were sealed (Halvard stands on one of them) until only this one was left. Eldrasil's independence is its freedom from demon rule.
The demons: since the Demon King fell they have had no master. They are what demons are without one: wild, brutal and endless, with no plan beyond the next kill.
Now: Norvaine borders it and has held the demon front for as long as Norvaine has stood. It is a stalemate: Norvaine cannot push into the Demon Kingdom, and the demons cannot break Norvaine. One nation can hold the line only because nothing on the other side leads them.
Legend: the first Gate was opened by the mortal of the First Bargain, who became the Demon King. The Four Who Saved the World slew him, and could not close it.
Status: nobody has crossed the Gate and come back to describe the other side.

431.content:
[Skydock] A broad walled stone platform on the bay's south-west headland, where airships rest in wooden cradles beside their mooring masts, with a customs shed where a single bored Yozakuran clerk stamps everything. Every arrival and departure musters here. A switchback cliff road climbs from it along the west headland to the Lighthouse.
Feel: salt wind, gulls, ropes creaking.
At night: The masts and the platform are lit like a row of lanterns, lamps mark the cliff road all the way up to the Lighthouse, and the city's glow fills the whole bay below.
Feel at night: warm wind, distant music.

432.content:
[Fish Market] The city's seafood heart on the wharf: a long open hall where the morning catch is sold off ice and cooked on the spot, and the streets around it given over to grills, steamers and noodle stalls. Skewered prawns, grilled octopus, crab in chilli, coconut rice in leaf parcels, shaved ice in fruit syrup. Cheap by Sunreach standards, loud, and the best food on the island.
Feel: smoke, salt, shouting.
At night: Red paper lanterns and rune-lit signs over a hundred steaming stalls, low wooden stools in the street, and the cooks still shouting until three in the morning.
Feel at night: steam, sizzle, red light.

433.content:
[Sea Dock] The working dock beside the Fish Market where the fishing fleet ties up and the tour boats leave for the open sea: whale and dolphin tours in the morning, deep-sea fishing at noon, a dusk cruise at sunset. Nets drying, crates of ice, crews calling the next departure.
Feel: tar, nets, gulls.
At night: The fishing boats come in under their lamps and unload straight into the market.
Feel at night: lamps on water, wet planks.

434.content:
[The Hanabira] Halvard's hotel for the Trip: a long white Yozakuran beachfront hotel of five storeys with paper lanterns on every balcony, a lobby of pale wood and koi pools, a garden of flowering trees, and a hot spring bath on the roof. Postcards at the front desk.
Feel: cool wood, quiet water, polite bows.
At night: The lanterns glow on every balcony, and from the rooftop bath the whole lit city is laid out across the bay.
Feel at night: lantern light, steam, distant city noise.

435.content:
[Coral Beach] The white beach in front of the hotels, a long curve of fine sand and gentle surf, striped umbrellas, rented loungers and beach volleyball nets. Lifeguards in red until sunset; half the people on it are some shade of sunburnt.
Feel: hot sand, bright, waves.
At night: Beach clubs open under coloured rune lamps, fire dancers spin on the sand to drums, and the lit skyline doubles itself in the wet sand at the water's edge.
Feel at night: drums, firelight, warm sand.

436.content:
[Sunpier] An amusement pier running far out over the bay: a carousel, games of skill with stuffed prizes, a hall of mirrors, ice cream and Sunfizz stands, caricature artists, and the Gull Run, a little wooden roller coaster that swings out over the water. Sunreach's family side at its loudest.
Feel: screams, sugar, sea spray.
At night: The pier is outlined in rune lamps from end to end, fortune tellers set up between the games, and the Gull Run goes out over black water.
Feel at night: lights, screams, black water.

437.content:
[Tidehouse Aquarium] A domed glass aquarium at the pier's root: a walk-through tunnel under a tank of reef fish, rays and a slow old sea turtle everyone names. Quiet, cool and dim, the best place on the island to escape the heat.
Feel: blue, cool, hushed.
At night: Open late with the tank lit violet by rune lamps and jellyfish glowing in the dark; a favourite date.
Feel at night: violet glow, whispers.

438.content:
[Sunreach Crossing] The heart of the city, a vast crossroads where six streets meet under walls of huge painted banners (suns, waves, swirls of colour) and shopfronts: fashion boutiques, fruit-juice bars, game halls, a stand of horse carriages, and a clock tower everybody uses as a meeting point, where the Skyrail starts up the hill. By day it is busy and colourful.
Feel: crowds, bright paint, movement.
At night: Every banner glows under rune lamps and every shop sign burns in rune-lit glass; when the crossing keepers drop their flags, a thousand people cross at once in every direction. Street fashion, buskers, portrait sketchers, game halls open all night, and the noise never drops.
Feel at night: colour, footsteps, a sea of faces.

439.content:
[Velvet Lanes] A tangle of narrow alleys behind the Crossing, packed with tiny bars of six seats each, stacked two and three storeys high and reached by steep outside stairs; singing rooms with a hired lute player, smoky grills, fortune tellers, a night market selling anything (charms, forged papers, potions no apothecary at home would stock), and further in the pleasure houses behind silk curtains. Shuttered and sleepy by day.
Feel: shuttered, narrow, stale smoke.
At night: The brightest, densest, loudest few streets in the world: every sign competes in rune-lit glass, touts call from every door, and a group can lose each other in ten steps.
Feel at night: rune-glow, smoke, whispers, too close.

440.content:
[The Golden Tide] The biggest casino resort on the island, a domed tower of gold and blue glass with a great golden sea serpent coiled up its whole front, and a round lake of fountains at its feet: dice, cards and the great wheel on a floor of nobles, crime lords and tourists, and house dealers who never smile. It does not check a bracelet or ask an age. By day it is half-asleep: cleaners, gamblers who never went to bed, and cool air at the doors.
Feel: cool air, chips clicking, gold.
At night: Every hour the house's water mages throw the lake into fountains higher than the tower in time to an orchestra on the terrace, the tables are full to the walls, and the doors swallow the whole street.
Feel at night: fountains, roar of the tables, gold and red.
<narrator_only>Ottavio Bastiani was floor boss here for nearly forty years. The older dealers and doormen still speak of "Signor Bastiani" with respect and some fear; a student who mentions him, or a Sky student who carries themselves like one, is treated very carefully. Nobody here will say what else he did for the house.</narrator_only>

441.content:
[Plaza Dourada] An old colonial square beside the casinos, from the days before the island sold itself to pleasure: pastel arcaded buildings, a wave-patterned black-and-white mosaic pavement, a fountain, and pastry shops selling custard tarts and almond cookies. Quiet and charming by day.
Feel: pastel, mosaic, sweet pastry.
At night: The square is ringed by the casino towers' light and filled with tourists drifting in from the tables; the pastry shops stay open and the fountain is lit gold.
Feel at night: gold light, old stone, the casinos' glow.

442.content:
[The Terraces] The island's own town, built up the steep hillside behind the city in layers: streets stacked on streets, stairways, alley markets and houses on tall timber stilts clinging to the cliff, so that the ground floor of one street is the roof of the next; old stone aqueducts arch across the ravines between the hills. Spice stalls, woven hats, shell jewellery, fruit nobody can name, aloe salve, and cafés where the locals play dominoes. Cheaper and friendlier than anywhere on the beach.
Feel: stairs, spice, laundry lines, shade.
At night: The whole hillside lights up layer by layer, the stilt houses glowing gold over the city like a stacked lantern; hot-pot restaurants spill onto every landing.
Feel at night: chilli steam, gold light, a long way down.

443.content:
[Skyrail] Little red cable cars drawn by rune-engines on a long cable from the clock tower at the Crossing up over the stilt houses to the summit by the Old Fort, passing through a station built right into a house halfway up. Everyone takes the same sketch of it.
Feel: rattling, windy, a view.
At night: The cabins glow as they swing up over the lit terraces, and the whole city opens out below.
Feel at night: vertigo, light everywhere below.

444.content:
[Old Fort] A ruined sea fort at the top of the hill: crumbling walls, rusted cannons and goats; the best view of the whole bay, and on a clear day of the open sea.
Feel: wind, quiet, old stone.
At night: Dark and quiet above the glowing city; the one place in Sunreach where the stars show.
Feel at night: dark, stars, the city humming below.

445.content:
[The Lagoon] A shallow lagoon of startling turquoise behind the reef on the eastern headland, warm as a bath, with floating rafts, rented paddle boats, and a beach bar on stilts over the water with thatched huts on its jetties, serving coconut drinks.
Feel: turquoise, warm water, laughter.
At night: The rafts are strung with rune lamps and the beach bar plays slow music; the water is black and still.
Feel at night: small lights, black water, slow music.

446.content:
[Reef Gardens] The coral reef at the lagoon's mouth: glass-bottom boats on the hour, snorkels for hire, and pearl divers who show off for coins. The colours are like nothing in Eldrasil.
Feel: colour, salt, sunlight through water.
At night: The boats stop; the reef's edge glows faintly where the plankton stirs.
Feel at night: dark, faint glow.

447.content:
[Shell Cove] A small hidden cove at the tip of the eastern headland, beyond the rocks at the lagoon's far end and reached by a path through the palms: pink shell sand, a single crooked palm leaning over the water, and nobody else.
Feel: secret, pink sand, quiet.
At night: Moonlight on the shells and the city's glow on the far side of the bay.
Feel at night: moonlight, waves, alone together.

448.content:
[The Lighthouse] A tall white lighthouse at the top of the west headland, reached by the switchback cliff road from the Skydock; open to climb by day for a coin. The keeper is a retired Norvaine sailor who tells storm stories to anyone who listens.
Feel: wind, white paint, endless sea.
At night: The beam sweeps the sea and the lit city both; the keeper lets nobody up after dark.
Feel at night: the beam, the dark sea.

449.content:
[Sunset Cliffs] The cliffs below the lighthouse where the whole island comes to watch the sun go down into the sea. Locals and the brave dive from the lower ledges into deep clear water; the Trip's most famous confessions happen here at dusk.
Feel: gold light, height, held breath.
At night: The crowd goes back to the city; the cliffs are dark and windy.
Feel at night: wind, dark, surf below.

450.content:
[Glowtide Grotto] A sea cave in the cliff foot. A boatman rows visitors in through a low arch at the water line and along a winding tunnel where the water glows blue wherever an oar touches it, until the tunnel opens into a great cavern. There the boat ties up on a broad shore of smooth rock that can be walked on all the way round. In the middle lies a still round pool whose water glitters like scattered stars, and high above, the whole ceiling is covered in glowing plants, hanging moss and vines that shed a soft blue-green light over everything. Voices echo; nobody talks loudly for long. Boatmen charge a few coins and wait as long as you like.
Feel: blue-green glow, echo, cool stone, glittering water.
At night: Outside it is dark, inside it is exactly the same, only quieter; the boatmen charge double after dark.
Feel at night: glow, stillness, the sea breathing outside.

451.content:
[Open Sea] The deep water beyond the bay, an hour out by tour boat from the Sea Dock: morning tours to watch whales and dolphins, deep-sea fishing with the crew's rods, and a slow dusk cruise. The island shrinks to a line, then to nothing. Sailors here say the Leviathan has always lived somewhere under these waters and that, once in a lifetime, it lets itself be seen.
Feel: blue on blue, sun, deep swell.
At night: Only the dusk cruise is out; the city glows on the horizon like a jewel.
Feel at night: dark swell, a glowing horizon.

452.content: [High Dovecote] The headquarters of the Doves, a white tower with a walled courtyard of grey uniforms. The public may stand at its gate; nobody walks in. Mages in academy uniform are noticed here.

453.content: [Royal Bank] The kingdom's bank behind a long white colonnade, where Halvard's Banking House sends its ledgers. Coin changed, accounts opened, loans signed. The Arslan World Bank keeps an office in the same street.

454.content:
[Skyport] Airship masts and a paved landing field just outside the Great Gate, the main gate in the south wall, with the customs hall and the passenger halls inside it. Every academy trip lands and musters here.
Feel: Masts, balloon envelopes and the whole city rising in front of you.

455.content: [Gilded Arcade] Two glass-roofed shopping arcades either side of Crown Avenue, just inside the Great Gate. Ardenne's flagship store, the original Merryhew's, Firetooth's own sweet shop, cafés, tailors and jewellers. Expensive, polished, and the first thing most visitors see.

456.content:
[Lantern Market] Avalon's biggest market: covered streets and a glass market hall hung with paper lanterns that are lit at dusk. Food from every province, cheap clothes, charms, imported goods, street performers, pickpockets.
Feel: Lanterns, awnings, shouting, frying, and your purse to watch.

457.content: [Spellwright Row] The street of the magic trades. Staff and wand makers, component sellers, enchanters, rune engravers, spellbook dealers, a shop for duelling gear. Stock the academy Mall never carries, at capital prices; every shop holds a Doves licence on the wall.

458.content:
[Old Town] The one grey quarter: narrow crooked lanes of grey stone from before independence, taverns, old bookshops, fortune tellers, the cheapest food in the city. Easy to get lost in. Everyone in Avalon has heard that somewhere in Old Town a door leads down into the Rookery, the city's underbelly; nobody respectable admits to knowing which one.
Feel: Grey stone, crooked lanes, and doors nobody talks about.

459.content:
[Skywheel Fair] A permanent fairground on the old parade ground at the edge of Old Town. Its giant wheel, turned by magitech, gives the second-best view in Avalon after the Great Spire and is the city's favourite place for a date; around it, games of skill with prizes, sweet stalls, a carousel and fortune booths. Busiest on holidays and at dusk, when the wheel lights up.
Feel: Music, sugar, and the city tilting below the wheel.

460.content: [The Great Spire] The tallest of the seven Herald Spires and the oldest, a slender white tower inside the north wall with a public viewing gallery near the top (a small fee in coin; a long stair or the lift). From the gallery the whole white city lies in its rings.

461.content:
[Garden of Avalon] The city's great public garden: lawns, flower terraces, a long reflecting pool and shaded walks, busiest on holidays. At its centre stands the Archmage, the largest statue in Eldrasil: a figure in white stone, taller than the trees, staff raised over four seals cut into the ground around the plinth. The face under the hood is smooth and the plinth carries no name, because no record keeps either; visitors argue about it.
Feel: Flowers, still water, and a hero with no face.

462.content: [Grand Theatre] The domed white opera house of the capital beside the garden. Opera, plays and concerts; on Crowning Day a cheap afternoon matinee for the holiday crowd.

463.content:
[Royal Arena] The open-air stadium of the kingdom, white stone tiers round a sand floor, warded for magic duels; the Kingdom Competition is fought here. Great scrying crystals hang above the tiers and show the crowd the rounds fought away from the sand; beneath the sand lies the Undercroft. On other days: tournaments, races, shows.
Feel: Ten thousand seats and the sand where reputations are made.

464.content: [Whitestone Hotel] The grand hotel beside the arena where the four academies' Kingdom Competition teams stay. Doormen, a lobby that never sleeps, a courtyard fountain, and a dining room where rival teams pretend not to look at each other.

465.content: [AIRSHIP INDEX] Aboard the academy's airship: Promenade Deck (the glassed gallery and the view), Common Room (the canteen counter, a small bar, the stage), Cabin Deck (a cabin to each group of four, hot bathing stalls), Cargo Hold (luggage and gear, the most private corner). Two minutes apart; each place has its own entry when it comes up.

466.content:
[Avalon — the Kingsmeadow] The crown's meadowland beyond the Great Gate, thirty minutes' walk from the Skyport road: grass, a brook, an old orchard and a stone ring, warded at its edges by the competition panel. Round one of the Kingdom Competition is fought here, from dawn to sunset; on other days it is closed crown land.
Judges' Pavilion: A white pavilion with the royal blue and gold on its poles where the Kingsmeadow road meets the grass: the competition panel's table, the four academies' banners, a healer's tent beside it. Round one starts here at dawn, and here at sunset the judges take one Kingsbloom from each team.
Long Meadow: Waist-high grass rolling away from the pavilion in long waves, a few lone oaks, larks going up wherever someone walks. Everything moving out here can be seen from far off.
Willow Brook: A clear stream winding under old willows, stepping stones at the shallows and a footbridge of three planks; the banks are soft and keep footprints.
Old Orchard: Rows of old apple and pear trees from a royal estate long gone, gone half wild, windfalls in the grass and a collapsed press house at the end of the rows.
Bramble Hollow: A sunken hollow choked with bramble and blackthorn, narrow tracks through it that badgers made and nobody else can walk upright; the best place in the Kingsmeadow to wait unseen.
Standing Stones: A ring of eleven grey standing stones on a low rise, older than the kingdom; the panel's wards hum faintly between them, and the grass inside the ring is short and dry.
Reed Marsh: Reed beds taller than a person around pools of black water, duckboards laid by the panel along one line only; off them, it is wet to the knee and loud with every step.
Beacon Hill: The highest ground in the Kingsmeadow, crowned by an old beacon basket on a stone post; from the top the whole field shows, and so does whoever stands on it.

467.content:
[Avalon — the Undercroft] The old vaults under the Royal Arena, down a stair from the arena's west side: ten rooms around the Undercroft Gates, each holding a beast the competition panel has bound there for the day, the wards on every wall. Round two of the Kingdom Competition is fought here; on other days the stair is locked.
Undercroft Gates: A long vaulted hall at the foot of the stairs under the arena, warded lamps in brackets, and three iron gates into the Undercroft, one for each team still in. A board of ten sigils by the stairs lights a room's sigil in the colour of the team that holds it.
Undercroft Room 1: The Pillar Hall: a low hall of squat pillars close enough to touch, lamplight broken into stripes between them.
Undercroft Room 2: The Cistern: a flooded vault with a stone walkway round its edge and still black water in the middle.
Undercroft Room 3: The old Armoury: empty weapon racks on every wall, a broken portcullis half down across the far arch.
Undercroft Room 4: The sunken Chapel: three steps down to a stone floor, a plain altar, niches in the walls where candles once stood.
Undercroft Room 5: The Gallery: a narrow balcony room above a drop into darkness, a rail on one side, the wards glowing along the edge.
Undercroft Room 6: The Kennels: a row of barred stalls where the arena's beasts were kept between shows, straw still on the floor.
Undercroft Room 7: The Furnace room: a great cold furnace with an iron door, flues climbing into the dark, soot on every surface.
Undercroft Room 8: The Vault: a round room behind a door a hand thick, shelves cut into the stone, the air dry and still.
Undercroft Room 9: The Pit: a sand-floored fighting pit older than the arena above it, tiers of rough stone around it where a few hundred once watched.
Undercroft Room 10: The Deep Hall: the lowest and largest room, a vault so high the lamps do not reach its roof, and every sound comes back twice.

468.content:
HANAKAZE INDEX — the capital of Yozakura, host of the World Competition this year. Each place has its own entry when it comes up.
A city of wooden streets, red gates and snow. Every street is lined with sakura, bare now and heavy with snow, and at the city's heart stands the Eternal Sakura, in full bloom all year, its petals falling onto the snow. Mount Hakuho rises white on the horizon. Everyone bows, and everyone competes.
Skyport: Hanakaze Skyport, Red Tower Arcade. Castle hill: the Hall of Victors (banquets), the Alpha's Residence (closed). Sakura Park: the Eternal Sakura, Snow Festival Park, the Golden Pavilion. Victors' Avenue: the Challenge Crossing, Thunder Gate Temple. Old quarter: the Hundred Alleys, the Glass Canal, Forge Street, the Mask Theatre. Hell Valley Springs. Shrine hill: the Fox Gates, the Cliff Temple. By the park: the Crowning Ring (the Grand Final) and the Thousand Lantern Inn (every team lodges here).
Beyond the city, by team carriage on match days only: the Bamboo Sea (Phase 1), Old Castle Shiroyama (Phase 2).
Walks between the parts (minutes on foot, the same both ways; a place inside one part is five to ten minutes from the next):
Hanakaze Skyport: Victors' Avenue 15, The Crowning Ring 20, Sakura Park 25, Thunder Gate 35, Old Quarter 35, Castle Hill 40, Shrine Hill 40, Hell Valley 55.
Victors' Avenue: Sakura Park 10, Thunder Gate 20, Old Quarter 20, Castle Hill 25, The Crowning Ring 25, Shrine Hill 35, Hell Valley 40.
Sakura Park: Thunder Gate 10, Castle Hill 15, The Crowning Ring 15, Old Quarter 20, Shrine Hill 25, Hell Valley 40.
Thunder Gate: Castle Hill 10, Shrine Hill 15, The Crowning Ring 15, Old Quarter 30, Hell Valley 50.
Castle Hill: Shrine Hill 25, The Crowning Ring 25, Old Quarter 35, Hell Valley 55.
Shrine Hill: The Crowning Ring 20, Old Quarter 45, Hell Valley 65.
The Crowning Ring: Old Quarter 35, Hell Valley 55.
Old Quarter: Hell Valley 20.
The team carriage from the Thousand Lantern Inn: The Bamboo Sea 40 min, Old Castle Shiroyama 25 min. Points do not work in Yozakura; coin only.
Rules: free in the city until 21:00, back at the inn by 22:00. The Alpha's Residence is closed to every guest. Any fair challenge at the Challenge Crossing must be accepted. Who is met, street sights and the dice are the engine's, listed in <now>.

469.content:
[Hanakaze Skyport] The hub of Yozakura's airship lines: red mooring towers in a row along the bay, liners coming and going all day, and clerks who bow before they stamp.
Feel: Red towers, white balloons, and a clerk bowing before every stamp.

470.content: [Red Tower Arcade] A covered arcade beneath the mooring towers, where Yozakura's great service companies keep their flagship counters: the hotel chain behind The Hanabira at Sunreach, the airship lines, the bathhouse houses. Boxed winter sweets, folding umbrellas, lucky charms for the flight home.

471.content:
[The Challenge Crossing] The great five-way crossing on Victors' Avenue, the main street from the castle hill, lined with snow-laden sakura and a stone lantern for every Alpha. When the bell rings, the crowd crosses in every direction at once; on the clerks' platform in the middle, anyone may challenge anyone to a fair contest, from duels to eating matches, and a Tournament Office clerk records the result. A Yozakuran never refuses.
Feel: A bell, a thousand people moving at once, and someone always shouting a challenge.

472.content:
[The Eternal Sakura] A giant sakura at the heart of the city, wider than a house and older than the throne, in full bloom all year round. In winter its pink petals fall onto the snow beneath it, and the whole city comes to stand under it at least once. Nobody knows why it never stops flowering; Yozakurans say it will bloom as long as Yozakura has an Alpha.
Feel: Pink petals falling on white snow, and the whole crowd gone quiet.

473.content: [Snow Festival Park] The long park around the Eternal Sakura, given over this week to the snow festival: towering snow sculptures of past Alphas and champions, ice slides for children and students alike, and a sculpture of every competing team's ace, unveiled at the opening banquet.

474.content: [The Golden Pavilion] A gilded pavilion on a still pond at the park's far end, its golden roof white with snow and doubled in the water: the most painted view in Yozakura.

475.content:
[Thunder Gate Temple] The city's oldest temple behind a great red gate hung with one enormous paper lantern, guarded by carved thunder and wind gods. Fortune slips tied to every branch, a five-storey pagoda in the courtyard, and the narrow approach street before it selling grilled rice crackers, sweet bean cakes and fox masks.
Feel: Incense, grilled rice crackers, and fortune slips fluttering on every branch.

476.content:
[The Hall of Victors] The Alpha's great hall on the castle hill, where the opening and closing banquets are held. The name of every Alpha is carved into its pillars, the newest still bright; the government's offices and the Tournament Office fill the wooden wings below it.
Feel: Every Alpha's name carved in the pillars, the newest still bright.

477.content: [The Alpha's Residence] Behind the Hall, closed to every guest. Whoever holds the throne lives here until someone takes it from them.

478.content:
[The Fox Gates] A mountain path through thousands of red gates, one after another, climbing through the snow; stone foxes guard every turn, and Yozakurans leave offerings for luck before a fight.
Feel: A red tunnel through the snow, and a stone fox at every turn.

479.content: [The Cliff Temple] A wooden temple built out over a ravine on great timber stilts, its veranda the city's best view: the bay, the rooftops white with snow, the pink crown of the Eternal Sakura, and Mount Hakuho on the horizon.

480.content:
[The Crowning Ring] The arena where the Alpha is crowned by tournament: a stone ring under open sky, tiered galleries for thirty thousand, and great starglass scrying crystals that carry the final to every capital.
Feel: Thirty thousand seats around a ring of bare stone.

481.content:
[The Thousand Lantern Inn] A vast wooden inn beside the Ring, of the same company that runs The Hanabira, where every team lodges, one wing each. Paper screens, polished corridors, staff who remember every guest's name, hot springs in a walled garden under snow-laden sakura, and a dining hall where six nations eat breakfast within earshot of each other.
Feel: Paper screens, polished corridors, and six nations at breakfast within earshot.

482.content:
[The Hundred Alleys] A knot of lanes so narrow two people cannot pass, packed with a hundred tiny stalls that seat six at most: noodle broth simmered since dawn, skewers over charcoal, sake by the cup, smoke and laughter spilling into the snow. Every stall owner knows every regular.
Feel: Broth simmered since dawn, charcoal smoke, and laughter spilling into the snow.

483.content: [The Glass Canal] An old canal lined with stone warehouses turned into glass-blowing workshops and music-box shops, where visitors can blow their own glass; at night in winter, hundreds of candles in snow lanterns light the path along the water.

484.content: [Forge Street] The katana smiths' street: the ring of hammers from dawn, blades cooling in snow-fed troughs, and swords far more visitors admire than can afford. The smiths test a buyer's hand before they sell, and register every blade they make.

485.content: [The Mask Theatre] Yozakura's great stage: painted faces, roaring actors, revolving sets and a crowd that shouts the famous lines along with the cast.

486.content:
[Hell Valley Springs] A steaming volcanic valley on the city's edge, sulphur vents hissing between the rocks and carved demon statues on the path, with bathhouses below fed by its waters. Yozakurans settle arguments here, in silence, by who leaves the hottest pool last.
Feel: Sulphur steam, hissing vents, and grim old men in the hottest pool.

487.content:
[Hanakaze — The Warrens]
The Warrens: Hanakaze's underbelly, a warren of old flood tunnels, sake cellars and smugglers' passages beneath the Hundred Alleys, older than the castle on the hill. Its people call themselves ronin, the masterless, a joke at the Alpha's expense. A black market (stolen goods, unregistered blades from smiths who will not sign them, forged Tournament Office records, contraband components), gambling dens that take bets on every challenge in the city, the Cellar Ring where fights are held that are anything but fair (no rules, no clerks, bets in cash), and brokers who sell information to anyone. Lantern-lit, crowded and polite in its own way: ronin do not rob guests who bow properly, and they never forget a face that brings the Alpha's Watch. Students are forbidden to go there. Buying or practising a forbidden art there is still arrest, as everywhere; a competitor caught there can be struck from the competition.
<narrator_only>The way in: behind the oldest noodle stall in the Hundred Alleys; the cook lifts the curtain at the back for anyone who orders "the bottom of the pot". A few alley regulars will point the way for coin; nobody else will. The Alpha's Watch raids the Warrens now and then (the engine decides when, in <now>), and the ronin usually hear it coming.</narrator_only>

488.content: [Hanakaze — The Bamboo Sea] A vast bamboo forest beyond the city, its stalks bowed under snow, ringed for the competition by a barrier that closes in all day. Phase 1 of the World Competition, Last Team Standing, is fought here, on Tue and Wed of the competition week; the team carriages leave the Thousand Lantern Inn on those days, and on other days the ground is closed.

489.content: [Hanakaze — Old Castle Shiroyama] A ruined white hill castle from the age of warring lords, stone walls and gates still standing; its two ward stones are the Siege's targets. Phase 2 of the World Competition, the Siege, is fought here, on Thu and Fri of the competition week; the team carriages leave the Thousand Lantern Inn on those days, and on other days the ground is closed.
